category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Distinguish the fate of the 4th pharyngeal pouch's ventral wing from its dorsal wing.
back:
### 4th Pouch Differentiation
* **Dorsal wing:** Forms the superior parathyroid gland (attaches to thyroid).
* **Ventral wing:** Forms the ultimobranchial body (gives rise to calcitonin-secreting C-cells).

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Trace the embryological origin of accessory thymic tissue sometimes found in the neck.
back:
### Ectopic Thymic Tissue
* Remnants left along the 3rd pouch migratory path.
* Path extends from the neck to the anterior mediastinum.
* Often found near or embedded in the thyroid.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: The [___] is a transient, ectoderm-lined cavity formed when the second pharyngeal arch overgrows the third and fourth arches during the fifth week of development.
back:
• Cervical Sinus
• Normally obliterated during growth
• Persistence leads to lateral cervical (branchial) cysts

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A neonate presents with hypocalcemic seizures, recurrent fungal infections, and a truncated aortic arch. Identify the embryological failure associated with this presentation.
back:
• Failure of the 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches to differentiate
• Diagnosis: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion)
• Results in thymic aplasia and parathyroid hypoplasia

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Explain the role of the second pharyngeal arch in the formation of an external branchial fistula.
back:
• Failure of the 2nd arch to grow caudally over the 3rd and 4th arches
• Remnants of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th clefts remain in contact with the surface
• Usually opens anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Contrast the underlying causes and primary mandibular defects of Treacher Collins syndrome and Robin sequence.
back:
• Treacher Collins: TCOF1 mutation; zygomatic/malar hypoplasia
• Robin sequence: Often a deformation (e.g., oligohydramnios); triad of micrognathia, glossoptosis, and cleft palate

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Identify the specific pharyngeal pouch that gives rise to the inferior parathyroid glands and explain their relative adult position.
back:
• Derived from the 3rd pharyngeal pouch
• They migrate caudally with the thymus
• End up inferior to the superior parathyroids (which derive from the 4th pouch)

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Diagnosis of DiGeorge syndrome is confirmed by detecting a microdeletion on chromosome [___].
back:
• 22q11.2
• Disrupts neural crest cell migration
• Essential for pharyngeal apparatus development

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A 12-year-old patient presents with a slow-growing, painless mass at the angle of the mandible, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Identify the most likely embryological remnant.
back:
• Lateral Cervical (Branchial) Cyst
• Remnant of the cervical sinus
• Often becomes evident in late childhood due to fluid accumulation

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
coreConcept: Neural Crest Role in Pharyngeal Glands
front: Describe how neural crest cell disruption results in the combined glandular and skeletal defects seen in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
back:
• Neural crest cells provide mesenchyme for pharyngeal arches
• Disruption prevents endodermal-mesenchymal interactions
• Prevents normal differentiation of pouch-derived thymus and parathyroid glands

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Distinguish between a thyroglossal duct cyst and a branchial cyst based on anatomical orientation.
back:
• Thyroglossal Cyst: Midline location (usually near hyoid bone)
• Branchial Cyst: Lateral location (anterior to sternocleidomastoid muscle)

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: List the primary skeletal derivatives of the first pharyngeal arch that are typically hypoplastic in Treacher Collins syndrome.
back:
• Maxilla and Mandible
• Zygomatic bone
• Middle ear ossicles (Malleus and Incus)

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: During neck development, the second pharyngeal arch overgrows the third and fourth arches, creating an ectoderm-lined cavity called the [___], which normally disappears.
back:
Cervical sinus
- Formed by the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th pharyngeal clefts.
- Failure to obliterate results in a lateral cervical (branchial) cyst.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A neonate presents with micrognathia, a posteriorly placed tongue, and a cleft palate (Robin sequence). Which pharyngeal arch is primarily affected in this developmental anomaly?
back:
First Pharyngeal Arch
- Specifically involves the mandibular prominence.
- Posterior tongue prevents fusion of palatal shelves, causing a cleft palate.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Explain the role of the third pharyngeal pouch endoderm in the development of the thymus and parathyroid glands.
back:
Differential Pouch Migration:
- Dorsal wing: Differentiates into the inferior parathyroid gland.
- Ventral wing: Forms the thymus.
- Thymus migrates caudally, pulling the inferior parathyroid with it.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Contrast the anatomical location of a lateral cervical cyst with a thyroglossal duct cyst.
back:
Anatomical Differentiation:
- Lateral Cervical Cyst: Lateral neck, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
- Thyroglossal Cyst: Midline of the neck, typically near the hyoid bone.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Describe the embryological defect causing the hypocalcemia and T-cell deficiency seen in DiGeorge Syndrome.
back:
Deletion 22q11.2
- Failure of the 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches to differentiate.
- Results in parathyroid hypoplasia (hypocalcemia) and thymic aplasia (immune deficiency).

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Internal branchial fistulas are rare and typically result from a rupture of the membrane between the second pharyngeal cleft and the [___].
back:
Second Pharyngeal Pouch
- These fistulas usually open into the tonsillar region.
- Result from persistence of the second cleft/pouch connection.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: An infant is born with mandibular hypoplasia, malformed ears, and zygomatic arch defects. Which specific cell population failed to migrate to the first pharyngeal arch?
back:
Neural Crest Cells
- Form the viscerocranium and skeletal elements.
- Defects lead to Treacher Collins syndrome (Mandibulofacial dysostosis).

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: How do ectopic parathyroid glands occur during embryogenesis and where are they most commonly found?
back:
Migration Pathway Remnants:
- Glands fail to stop at the thyroid's dorsal surface.
- Inferior parathyroids are highly variable and may be found at the carotid bifurcation.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Distinguish between the origin and derivatives of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches regarding laryngeal innervation.
back:
Laryngeal Nerve Supply:
- Fourth Arch: Superior laryngeal nerve (innervates cricothyroid).
- Sixth Arch: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (innervates intrinsic laryngeal muscles).

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: List the derivatives of the fourth pharyngeal pouch.
back:
Derivatives include:
- Superior parathyroid glands.
- Ultimobranchial body (gives rise to parafollicular C-cells of the thyroid).

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The five facial prominences, appearing at the end of the fourth week, consist primarily of mesenchyme derived from [___] cells.
back:
Neural crest cells
* These cells migrate from the neuroectoderm into the pharyngeal arches.
* They are essential for the formation of the facial skeleton and connective tissues.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a visible cleft running from the medial corner of the eye down to the upper lip, with the nasolacrimal duct exposed to the surface. Identify the embryological failure.
back:
Oblique Facial Cleft
* Failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with the corresponding lateral nasal prominence.
* Occurs along the line of the nasolacrimal groove.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Outline the process by which the nasolacrimal duct transforms from a surface groove into a functional canal.
back:
Canalization of the Ectodermal Cord
* Ectoderm in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid cord.
* The cord detaches from the surface ectoderm.
* Subsequent canalization forms the duct; the upper end widens into the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological defects resulting in a common lateral cleft lip versus a rare median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
Lateral vs. Median Cleft Lip
* Lateral: Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence.
* Median: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences in the midline.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the facial prominences that merge to form the intermaxillary segment.
back:
Merged Medial Nasal Prominences
* Formed as maxillary prominences grow medially.
* Consists of the philtrum (labial component), primary palate, and the four incisor teeth area.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The [___] prominence is a single, unpaired structure that gives rise to the forehead and the bridge of the nose.
back:
Frontonasal prominence
* It forms the upper border of the stomodeum.
* It later develops nasal placodes under the inductive influence of the forebrain.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A child presents with a small, narrow head and a single central eye (cyclopia). This defect is typically associated with which underlying midline tissue loss?
back:
Holoprosencephaly
* Caused by the loss of midline tissue (e.g., via SHH mutations or alcohol exposure).
* Prevents the separation of the eye fields and proper frontonasal development.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the role of the maxillary prominences in the definitive formation of the upper lip.
back:
Upper Lip Formation
* Maxillary prominences grow medially and fuse with medial nasal prominences.
* They form the lateral portions of the upper lip.
* Medial nasal prominences contribute the philtrum.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the adult derivatives of the medial nasal prominence and the lateral nasal prominence.
back:
Nasal Prominence Derivatives
* Medial: Forms the philtrum of the upper lip, and the crest and tip of the nose.
* Lateral: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three main components that contribute to the formation of the nose.
back:
Frontonasal, Medial Nasal, and Lateral Nasal Prominences
* Frontonasal: Bridge of the nose.
* Medial Nasal: Crest and tip.
* Lateral Nasal: Alae.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: The second pharyngeal arch grows caudally over the third and fourth arches, normally obliterating the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th pharyngeal clefts to form a temporary ectoderm-lined cavity called the [___].
back:
• Cervical Sinus
• Formed by the overgrowth of the 2nd arch.
• Normally disappears; persistence leads to lateral cervical (branchial) cysts.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A neonate presents with a small mouth, micrognathia, low-set ears, and tetralogy of Fallot. Laboratory tests reveal severe hypocalcemia. Identify the likely embryological defect.
back:
• DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion)
• Failure of 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches to differentiate.
• Results in thymic aplasia (immune deficiency) and parathyroid hypoplasia (hypocalcemia).

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Explain the embryological basis of an external branchial fistula opening on the lateral aspect of the neck anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
• Failure of the 2nd pharyngeal arch to grow caudally over the 3rd and 4th arches.
• This leaves remnants of the 2nd–4th clefts in contact with the surface via a narrow canal.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A patient presents with a neck mass. Contrast the typical anatomical location and movement of a Thyroglossal Duct Cyst versus a Lateral Cervical Cyst.
back:
• Thyroglossal Cyst: Midline location; moves with tongue protrusion or swallowing.
• Lateral Cervical Cyst: Lateral location (anterior to sternocleidomastoid); does not move with tongue protrusion.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Describe the triad of physical findings in Robin Sequence and the specific 1st arch developmental failure that initiates them.
back:
• Triad: Micrognathia, glossoptosis (posterior tongue), and U-shaped cleft palate.
• Primary defect: Poor mandible growth prevents the tongue from descending, blocking palatal shelf fusion.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: In DiGeorge Syndrome, mutations or deletions in the [___] gene disrupt the epithelial-mesenchymal interactions between pharyngeal pouch endoderm and neural crest mesenchyme.
back:
• TBX1 (T-box DNA binding transcription factor 1)
• Regulates development of the pharyngeal apparatus.
• Essential for thymus, parathyroid, and cardiac outflow tract formation.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: A child is diagnosed with Treacher Collins syndrome (mandibulofacial dysostosis). Which skeletal derivatives of the 1st pharyngeal arch are most likely to be hypoplastic or absent?
back:
• Maxilla, mandible, and zygomatic arches.
• Also involves middle ear ossicles (malleus and incus).
• Caused by TCOF1 mutations affecting neural crest cell proliferation.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Why are ectopic parathyroid glands derived from the 3rd pharyngeal pouch more frequently found in the lower neck or thorax than those from the 4th pouch?
back:
• Inferior parathyroids (3rd pouch) migrate caudally with the thymus.
• They have a longer migratory path, increasing the chance of being pulled to the mediastinum or carotid bifurcation.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Contrast the origins of the superior and inferior parathyroid glands by their respective pharyngeal pouches.
back:
• Superior Parathyroid: Dorsal wing of the 4th pharyngeal pouch.
• Inferior Parathyroid: Dorsal wing of the 3rd pharyngeal pouch.

category: Discuss the embryological basis of congenital anomalies related to the development of pharyngeal arches, pharyngeal clefts and pharyngeal pouches: cervical sinus/fistula/cyst, 1st arch syndrome, DiGeorge syndrome, congenital malformations of thymus and parathyroid glands
front: Identify the pharyngeal pouch derivative responsible for the development of Parafollicular (C) cells of the thyroid gland.
back:
• Ultimobranchial body (from the ventral wing of the 4th pouch).
• Later incorporated into the thyroid gland.
• Secrete calcitonin to regulate blood calcium levels.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
coreConcept: Derivatives of the Medial Nasal Prominence
front: The philtrum of the upper lip is derived from the merged [___] nasal prominences.
back:
* Medial nasal prominences
* These prominences form the intermaxillary segment
* Fusion occurs at the midline during the 7th week

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: An infant is born with a facial cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the mouth. Identify the developmental failure involved.
back:
* Failure of maxillary and lateral nasal prominences to merge
* Involves the nasolacrimal groove
* Results in an oblique facial cleft exposing the duct

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Summarize the cellular transformation that occurs within the nasolacrimal groove to form its associated drainage duct.
back:
* Surface ectoderm forms a solid epithelial cord
* Cord detaches from overlying ectoderm
* Canalization of the cord creates the functional duct

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Differentiate the embryological basis of a common unilateral cleft lip from that of a rare midline (median) cleft lip.
back:
* Unilateral: Maxillary and medial nasal prominences fail to fuse
* Midline: Two medial nasal prominences fail to merge
* Midline often signals brain defects like holoprosencephaly

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three anatomical components formed by the intermaxillary segment during facial development.
back:
* Philtrum of the upper lip
* Upper jaw component (bearing four incisors)
* Triangular primary palate

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The adult nasolacrimal duct drains from the medial corner of the eye into the [___] of the nasal cavity.
back:
* Inferior meatus
* Proximal end widens to form the lacrimal sac
* Distal end connects to the nasal airway

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a single central eye (cyclopia) and a midline facial deficit. Explain the molecular signaling failure linked to this presentation.
back:
* Loss of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling
* Failure to separate the single eye field into two
* Associated with holoprosencephaly and loss of midline tissue

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the role of neural crest cells in the population of the five facial prominences.
back:
* Migrate from the neuroectoderm (midbrain/hindbrain)
* Form the underlying mesenchyme of the prominences
* Vulnerable to teratogens like alcohol and retinoic acid

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the adult nasal derivatives of the medial nasal prominences with those of the lateral nasal prominences.
back:
* Medial: Forms the bridge, crest, and tip of the nose
* Lateral: Forms the alae (wings/sides) of the nose

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the embryonic structures that form the lateral boundaries of the stomodeum by the end of the fourth week.
back:
* Maxillary prominences
* Derived from the dorsal portion of the first pharyngeal arch
* Later fuse with medial nasal prominences to form cheeks

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The philtrum of the upper lip is formed primarily from the [___] nasal prominences.
back:
*   Derived from the merged medial nasal prominences.
*   Forms part of the intermaxillary segment.
*   Also contributes the primary palate and four incisor teeth.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the upper lip, exposing the nasolacrimal duct. Identify the embryological failure.
back:
*   Diagnosis: Oblique facial cleft.
*   Mechanism: Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the lateral nasal prominence.
*   Result: Nasolacrimal duct remains exposed on the surface.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the embryological formation and canalization of the nasolacrimal duct.
back:
*   Originates as a solid ectodermal cord in the nasolacrimal groove.
*   Groove is between maxillary and lateral nasal prominences.
*   Cord detaches and canalizes; upper end widens to form the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological defects resulting in an anterior cleft lip versus a posterior cleft palate.
back:
*   Cleft Lip: Failure of maxillary prominence and medial nasal prominence to fuse.
*   Cleft Palate: Failure of palatine shelves (from maxillary processes) to meet in the midline.
*   Landmark: The incisive foramen divides anterior and posterior defects.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the structures derived from the frontonasal prominence during facial development.
back:
*   Forms the forehead.
*   Forms the bridge of the nose.
*   Gives rise to the nasal placodes and subsequent nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The [___] nasal prominences are the specific facial components that form the alae (sides) of the nose.
back:
*   Lateral nasal prominences.
*   They form the lateral boundaries of the nasal pits.
*   They do not participate in the formation of the upper lip.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A child is born with a midline (median) cleft lip. Explain the clinical significance regarding the underlying brain development.
back:
*   Failure: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
*   Clinical correlation: Often associated with holoprosencephaly.
*   Indicates severe loss of midline tissue/brain structures during neurulation.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the three-dimensional growth of the palatine shelves required for normal palate formation.
back:
*   Initially grow vertically on either side of the tongue.
*   Ascend to a horizontal position above the tongue in the 7th week.
*   Fuse with each other and the nasal septum.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryonic origins of the lower lip and jaw with those of the upper lip.
back:
*   Lower Lip/Jaw: Formed by the merging of paired mandibular prominences across the midline.
*   Upper Lip: Formed by fusion of two maxillary prominences and two medial nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Name the primitive ectodermal depression that becomes the mouth after the oropharyngeal membrane ruptures.
back:
*   Stomodeum.
*   Appears at the end of the 4th week.
*   Surrounded by the five mesenchymal facial prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two maxillary prominences with the two [___] prominences.
back:
- Medial nasal prominences.
- Occurs as maxillary prominences grow medially.
- Failure results in lateral cleft lip.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the mouth, exposing the nasolacrimal duct. This results from failure of fusion between which two prominences?
back:
- Maxillary prominence.
- Lateral nasal prominence.
- This is known as an oblique facial cleft.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the embryological process that forms the nasolacrimal duct.
back:
- Ectoderm in the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid cord.
- The cord detaches from the surface and canalizes to form a duct.
- The upper end widens to form the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological basis of a standard lateral cleft lip with that of a midline (median) cleft lip.
back:
- Lateral Cleft: Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence.
- Midline Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
- Midline clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three components derived from the intermaxillary segment.
back:
- Philtrum (labial component).
- Upper jaw (carrying four incisor teeth).
- Primary triangular palate.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The anatomical landmark dividing anterior cleft deformities from posterior cleft deformities is the [___].
back:
- Incisive foramen.
- Anterior clefts involve the lip and primary palate.
- Posterior clefts involve the secondary palate and uvula.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a small mandible, a posteriorly placed tongue (glossoptosis), and a cleft palate. Identify this sequence.
back:
- Robin sequence.
- Pathophysiology: Micrognathia prevents the tongue from dropping, blocking palatal shelf fusion.
- Often involves first-arch structures.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the mechanical transition the palatine shelves must undergo to form the secondary palate.
back:
- 6th Week: Shelves are vertical on either side of the tongue.
- 7th Week: Shelves ascend to a horizontal position above the tongue.
- Fusion: Shelves meet and fuse in the midline.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Differentiate the origins of the bridge of the nose from the alae (sides) of the nose.
back:
- Bridge: Derived from the frontonasal prominence.
- Alae: Derived from the lateral nasal prominences.
- Crest and Tip: Derived from merged medial nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the primary cellular source of the mesenchyme that forms the facial prominences.
back:
- Neural crest cells.
- They migrate from the neuroectoderm into the pharyngeal arches.
- Vulnerable to teratogens like alcohol and retinoic acid.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The nasolacrimal duct develops from a solid epithelial cord that originates in the floor of the [___] groove.
back:
• Nasolacrimal groove
• Located between the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences
• Cord canalizes to form the duct
• Upper end widens into the lacrimal sac

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a lateral gap in the upper lip. Name the specific mesenchymal prominences that failed to fuse to cause this defect.
back:
• Maxillary prominence
• Medial nasal prominence
• Occurs on one or both sides
• Failure of fusion results in a lateral cleft lip

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the role of the medial nasal prominences in the formation of the adult upper lip.
back:
• Merge at surface and deep levels
• Form the philtrum of the upper lip
• Fuse with the maxillary prominences laterally
• Contribute to the intermaxillary segment

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological failure of an oblique facial cleft with that of a standard lateral cleft lip.
back:
• Oblique Cleft: Maxillary prominence fails to fuse with the lateral nasal prominence
• Lateral Cleft Lip: Maxillary prominence fails to fuse with the medial nasal prominence
• Oblique clefts expose the nasolacrimal duct to the surface

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three anatomical components of the intermaxillary segment formed by the merged medial nasal prominences.
back:
• Labial component: Philtrum of upper lip
• Upper jaw component: Carries four incisor teeth
• Palatal component: Forms the triangular primary palate

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The alae (sides) of the nose are formed by the [___] nasal prominences.
back:
• Lateral nasal prominences
• These surround the nasal pits laterally
• Do not participate in upper lip formation
• Separated from maxillary prominences by the nasolacrimal groove

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a rare midline cleft in the upper lip. Identify the developmental failure and the major associated brain malformation.
back:
• Failure: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Associated Defect: Holoprosencephaly (loss of midline brain tissue)
• Often involves SHH signaling mutations

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the anatomical path of the nasolacrimal duct after it completes canalization.
back:
• Runs from the medial corner of the eye
• Descends through the facial mesenchyme
• Terminates in the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the structures formed by the frontonasal prominence and the mandibular prominences.
back:
• Frontonasal: Forehead, bridge of nose, and nasal placodes
• Mandibular: Lower lip, lower jaw (mandible), and chin
• Frontonasal is unpaired; Mandibular are paired

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the five mesenchymal prominences that surround the primitive stomodeum at the end of the fourth week.
back:
• Single frontonasal prominence (cranial)
• Paired maxillary prominences (lateral)
• Paired mandibular prominences (caudal)
• Primarily derived from neural crest-derived mesenchyme

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two maxillary prominences with the two [___].
back:
• Medial nasal prominences
• Note: Lateral nasal prominences do not participate in forming the lip
• Failure results in unilateral or bilateral cleft lip.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the upper lip, leaving the nasolacrimal duct exposed. Identify the embryological failure.
back:
• Oblique facial cleft
• Caused by failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with the lateral nasal prominence
• This failure occurs along the line of the nasolacrimal groove.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the role of the ectodermal cord in the development of the nasolacrimal duct.
back:
• Ectoderm in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid cord
• The cord detaches from the surface and canalizes to form the duct
• The upper end widens to form the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological basis of a standard lateral cleft lip with that of a median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
• Lateral Cleft: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominence fusion
• Median Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly and loss of midline tissue.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three anatomical derivatives of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
• Labial component (forms the philtrum)
• Upper jaw component (carries the four incisor teeth)
• Palatal component (forms the triangular primary palate).

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The bridge of the nose is derived from the [___] prominence.
back:
• Frontonasal prominence
• It also gives rise to the forehead
• Medial nasal prominences form the crest and tip.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A 1-week-old infant exhibits micrognathia, glossoptosis, and a secondary cleft palate. Identify the most likely clinical sequence.
back:
• Robin sequence
• Mechanism: Small mandible prevents the tongue from descending
• The tongue remains between palatal shelves, preventing their fusion.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the transition of the palatine shelves from the 6th to the 7th week of development.
back:
• 6th Week: Shelves are directed obliquely downward on each side of the tongue
• 7th Week: Shelves ascend to a horizontal position above the tongue
• Final step: Shelves fuse with each other and the primary palate.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish the contribution of the medial nasal prominence from the lateral nasal prominence in nasal formation.
back:
• Medial Nasal: Forms the crest and tip of the nose
• Lateral Nasal: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose
• Frontonasal: Forms the bridge.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Name the anatomical landmark that divides anterior cleft deformities from posterior cleft deformities.
back:
• Incisive foramen
• Anterior: Lateral cleft lip, cleft upper jaw
• Posterior: Cleft (secondary) palate, cleft uvula.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the paired maxillary prominences with the two [___] nasal prominences.
back:
• Medial nasal prominences
• Failure of this fusion results in lateral cleft lip
• Lateral nasal prominences are excluded from lip formation

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye down to the upper lip, leaving the nasolacrimal duct exposed. Identify the embryological failure.
back:
• Oblique facial cleft
• Failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with the lateral nasal prominence
• Occurs along the line of the nasolacrimal groove

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the process by which the nasolacrimal duct transitions from a surface feature to a canalized duct.
back:
• Ectoderm in the nasolacrimal groove floor forms a solid cord
• The cord detaches from the surface and canalizes
• Its upper end widens into the lacrimal sac

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological origin of a midline cleft lip with that of a common lateral cleft lip.
back:
• Median cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Lateral cleft: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominence fusion
• Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three specific anatomical derivatives of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
• Philtrum of the upper lip
• Premaxillary part of the maxilla (carries 4 incisors)
• Primary triangular palate

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The [___] prominence forms the forehead and the bridge of the nose, and is located cranial to the stomodeum.
back:
• Frontonasal prominence
• Formed by mesenchyme ventral to the brain vesicles
• Also gives rise to the nasal placodes

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: An infant is born with a split in the upper jaw between the lateral incisor and the canine tooth. Identify the landmark that divides this anterior cleft from posterior clefts.
back:
• Incisive foramen
• Anterior clefts involve the primary palate
• Posterior clefts involve the secondary (palatine shelves) palate

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the mechanical role of the maxillary prominences in the formation of the philtrum.
back:
• Maxillary prominences grow medially and increase in size
• They compress the medial nasal prominences toward the midline
• This forces the medial nasal prominences to merge into a single segment

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the adult nasal structures derived from the lateral versus medial nasal prominences.
back:
• Lateral nasal: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose
• Medial nasal: Forms the crest and tip of the nose
• Frontonasal: Forms the bridge

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the specific site within the nasal cavity where the nasolacrimal duct drains after canalization.
back:
• Inferior meatus
• Located on the lateral nasal wall
• Drainage is established after the meatal plug or cord canalizes

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
coreConcept: Ectodermal Origin of the Nasolacrimal Duct
front: The epithelial cord that eventually canalizes to form the nasolacrimal duct is derived from [___] found in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove.
back:
• Surface ectoderm
• Forms a solid cord that detaches from surface
• Canalizes to link the medial eye corner to the inferior nasal meatus.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a lateral gap in the upper lip extending toward the nostril. This defect results from a failure of fusion between which two specific prominences?
back:
• Maxillary prominence
• Medial nasal prominence
• Occurs during the 6th–7th weeks of development.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the biological mechanism that prevents the nasolacrimal duct from being exposed on the surface of the face during normal development.
back:
• Maxillary and lateral nasal prominences merge
• This burial of the nasolacrimal groove converts the ectodermal cord into an internal duct
• Detachment from surface ectoderm is required.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A 1-day-old infant is found to have an oblique facial cleft. Contrast this with a standard lateral cleft lip by identifying the anatomical furrow involved.
back:
• Oblique Cleft: Involves the nasolacrimal groove (between maxillary and lateral nasal prominences)
• Lateral Cleft Lip: Involves the junction between maxillary and medial nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the three components of the intermaxillary segment formed by the merging of the medial nasal prominences.
back:
• Labial: Philtrum of the upper lip
• Upper jaw: Carries four incisor teeth
• Palatal: Forms the triangular primary palate.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The single, unpaired facial structure that provides the mesenchyme for the forehead and bridge of the nose is the [___] prominence.
back:
• Frontonasal prominence
• Formed by mesenchyme ventral to the brain vesicles
• Gives rise to the nasal placodes.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
coreConcept: Median Cleft Lip and Midline Defects
front: An infant is born with a midline gap in the upper lip and synophthalmia (fused eyes). Identify the embryological failure associated with this presentation.
back:
• Median Cleft Lip
• Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Associated with holoprosencephaly and loss of midline tissue (SHH signaling).

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the specific roles of the medial and lateral nasal prominences in the formation of the definitive nose.
back:
• Medial nasal: Merge to form the crest and tip of the nose
• Lateral nasal: Form the alae (sides/wings) of the nose.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish the developmental origin of the lower lip from that of the upper lip.
back:
• Lower Lip: Fusion of the two mandibular prominences
• Upper Lip: Fusion of two maxillary prominences with two medial nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the embryological structure located between the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences that, if failing to close, results in an exposed nasolacrimal duct.
back:
• Nasolacrimal groove
• Extends from the medial corner of the eye to the oral cavity
• Failure of merging causes oblique facial clefts.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two maxillary prominences with the two [___] nasal prominences.
back:
● Medial.
● Fusion occurs as maxillary prominences grow medially and compress the medial nasal prominences toward the midline.
● Lateral nasal prominences do not participate in forming the upper lip.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a facial cleft running from the medial corner of the eye to the upper lip, with the nasolacrimal duct exposed. Identify the embryological defect.
back:
● Oblique facial cleft.
● Caused by failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with its corresponding lateral nasal prominence.
● This failure occurs along the line of the nasolacrimal groove.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the canalization process that leads to the formation of the nasolacrimal duct.
back:
● Ectoderm in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid epithelial cord.
● The cord detaches from the surface ectoderm.
● Subsequent canalization forms the duct, with the upper end widening to form the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological failures resulting in a lateral cleft lip versus a median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
● Lateral Cleft Lip: Partial or complete failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence.
● Median Cleft Lip: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences in the midline; often associated with holoprosencephaly.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the three specific components derived from the intermaxillary segment.
back:
● Labial component: Forms the philtrum of the upper lip.
● Upper jaw component: Carries the four incisor teeth.
● Palatal component: Forms the triangular primary palate.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The primary palate is derived from the intermaxillary segment, whereas the main part of the definitive palate is formed by [___].
back:
● Palatine shelves.
● These are shelflike outgrowths from the maxillary prominences.
● They appear in the sixth week and fuse to form the secondary palate.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A child presents with a cleft involving only the secondary palate. What is the most likely embryological basis for this isolated defect?
back:
● Lack of fusion of the palatine shelves.
● Possible causes include small shelves, failure of shelves to elevate, or the tongue failing to drop due to micrognathia.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Describe the positional changes the palatine shelves undergo between the sixth and seventh weeks of development.
back:
● 6th Week: Shelves are directed obliquely downward on each side of the tongue (vertical).
● 7th Week: Shelves ascend to a horizontal position above the tongue and fuse in the midline.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the contributions of the frontonasal, medial nasal, and lateral nasal prominences to the adult nose.
back:
● Frontonasal: Forms the bridge of the nose.
● Merged Medial Nasal: Provide the crest and the tip.
● Lateral Nasal: Form the alae (sides) of the nose.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: State the anatomical landmark that divides anterior and posterior cleft deformities.
back:
● Incisive foramen.
● Anterior clefts (e.g., cleft lip) are due to fusion failures with the primary palate.
● Posterior clefts involve the secondary palate and uvula.

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The philtrum of the upper lip is formed by the [___] component of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
• Labial component
• Derived from the fusion of the two medial nasal prominences
• Forms the central portion of the upper lip

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the upper lip, leaving the nasolacrimal duct exposed. Identify the embryological failure.
back:
• Oblique facial cleft
• Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the lateral nasal prominence
• Results in the nasolacrimal duct remaining as an open groove

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain the process of nasolacrimal duct formation from the nasolacrimal groove.
back:
• Ectoderm in the groove floor forms a solid epithelial cord
• Cord detaches and canalizes to form the duct
• Cranial end dilates to form the lacrimal sac
• Connects conjunctival sac to the inferior meatus

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological origins of the primary palate versus the secondary palate.
back:
• Primary Palate: Derived from the intermaxillary segment (fused medial nasal prominences)
• Secondary Palate: Formed by fusion of palatine shelves (maxillary prominence outgrowths)
• Landmark: Divided by the incisive foramen

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Identify the two specific prominences whose failure to merge results in a standard lateral cleft lip.
back:
• Maxillary prominence
• Medial nasal prominence
• Failure of mesenchymal bridge formation
• May be unilateral or bilateral

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: The bridge of the nose is formed by the [___] prominence.
back:
• Frontonasal prominence
• Unpaired structure cranial to the stomodeum
• Also gives rise to the forehead and nasal placodes

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: An infant presents with a midline cleft of the upper lip and associated holoprosencephaly. Name the embryological defect and its likely cause.
back:
• Median (midline) cleft lip
• Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Caused by deficiency of midline tissue
• Often associated with SHH signaling defects

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Explain how the maxillary prominences facilitate the narrowing of the early embryonic face.
back:
• Maxillary prominences enlarge and grow medially
• Push medial nasal prominences toward the midline
• Results in fusion of medial nasal prominences to form the philtrum
• Failure results in a wide-spaced appearance (hypertelorism)

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the structures formed by the lateral nasal prominence and the medial nasal prominence.
back:
• Lateral Nasal: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose
• Medial Nasal: Forms the crest, tip, and philtrum
• Both surround the nasal pits during week 5

category: Describe the development of face and nasolacrimal duct and their respective congenital anomalies
front: List the five mesenchymal prominences that surround the stomodeum to form the face.
back:
• One Frontonasal prominence
• Two Maxillary prominences
• Two Mandibular prominences
• All primarily derived from neural crest-derived mesenchyme

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The surface ectoderm thickenings on the frontonasal prominence that initiate the development of the nose are the [___].
back:
• Nasal (olfactory) placodes
• Formed under the inductive influence of the ventral forebrain
• Invaginate to form nasal pits during the 5th week

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A neonate presents with a unilateral cleft of the upper lip. This defect arises due to the failure of fusion between which two mesenchymal prominences?
back:
• Maxillary prominence
• Medial nasal prominence
• Failure of these to merge results in anterior cleft deformities

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the developmental transition from primitive choanae to definitive choanae in the nasal cavity.
back:
• Primitive: Openings behind the primary palate formed after the oronasal membrane breaks down
• Definitive: Located at the nasal-pharyngeal junction after secondary palate fusion

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the facial derivatives of the medial nasal prominence with those of the lateral nasal prominence.
back:
• Medial Nasal: Philtrum of the upper lip, crest of the nose, and tip of the nose
• Lateral Nasal: Alae (sides) of the nose

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Identify the embryological source and growth pattern of the paranasal air sinuses.
back:
• Source: Diverticula of the lateral nasal wall
• Pattern: Invade maxilla, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid bones
• Growth: Reach maximum size during puberty

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The primitive nasal cavity is initially separated from the oral cavity by the [___].
back:
• Oronasal membrane
• It breaks down to connect the nasal pits with the primitive oral cavity

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A newborn presents with a rare midline cleft lip. Specify the underlying embryological failure and associated risks.
back:
• Failure: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
• Risks: Often associated with cognitive impairment and brain defects (e.g., holoprosencephaly)

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Describe the formation and components of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
• Formation: Merging of the two medial nasal prominences at a deep level
• Components: Philtrum (labial), four incisor teeth (upper jaw), and primary palate (triangular)

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Distinguish between the primary and secondary palate based on their embryonic precursors.
back:
• Primary Palate: Derived from the intermaxillary segment (medial nasal prominences)
• Secondary Palate: Derived from palatine shelves (outgrowths of maxillary prominences)

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Name the structures formed by the frontonasal prominence in the developing face.
back:
• Forehead
• Bridge of the nose
• Medial nasal prominences
• Lateral nasal prominences

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: During the fifth week of development, local thickenings of surface ectoderm known as [___] invaginate under forebrain induction to form nasal pits.
back:
Nasal (olfactory) placodes.
- They form on the frontonasal prominence.
- Their invagination creates the medial and lateral nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A neonate presents with a tubular nose (proboscis) and a single central eye (cyclopia). This spectrum of defects originates from an early embryonic loss of [___].
back:
Midline tissue.
- Result of failed forebrain and frontonasal prominence development.
- Associated with holoprosencephaly.
- Often linked to SHH signaling disruption.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the embryological mechanism behind the formation and expansion of the paranasal sinuses.
back:
- Origin: Diverticula of the lateral nasal wall.
- Process: Pneumatization into the maxilla, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid bones.
- Timing: Reach maximum size during puberty, defining adult facial shape.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the primitive choanae with the definitive choanae in terms of their anatomical boundaries and formation.
back:
- Primitive: Located behind the primary palate; formed by oronasal membrane rupture.
- Definitive: Located at the junction of the nasal cavity and pharynx; formed after secondary palate fusion.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Identify the mesenchymal source and specific prominence that gives rise to the bridge of the nose.
back:
- Source: Neural crest-derived mesenchyme.
- Prominence: The frontonasal prominence (a single unpaired structure).

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The primitive nasal cavity is initially separated from the oral cavity by the [___], which must rupture to establish the primitive choanae.
back:
Oronasal membrane.
- Separates nasal pits from the oral cavity.
- Its breakdown establishes communication between the two cavities.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: An infant is born with an 'oblique facial cleft' where the nasolacrimal duct is exposed. This occurs due to failure of fusion between which two specific prominences?
back:
The Maxillary prominence and the Lateral nasal prominence.
- These fail to merge along the line of the nasolacrimal groove.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Describe the formation of the nasolacrimal duct from surface ectoderm.
back:
- Location: Ectoderm in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove.
- Process: Forms a solid epithelial cord that canalizes after detaching from ectoderm.
- Course: Runs from the medial eye corner to the inferior meatus.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Differentiate between the structural derivatives of the medial nasal prominences and the lateral nasal prominences.
back:
- Medial: Forms the crest, tip of the nose, and the philtrum of the upper lip.
- Lateral: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Specify the signaling molecule secreted by the prechordal plate that is essential for establishing the facial midline and separating the eye fields.
back:
Sonic Hedgehog (SHH).
- It upregulates PAX2 and downregulates PAX6 in the midline.
- Deficiencies lead to midline facial and brain malformations.

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: During the fifth week of development, the nasal placodes invaginate to form [___], which are the precursors to the primitive nasal cavities.
back:
• Nasal pits
• Formed by surface ectoderm invagination
• Surrounded by medial and lateral nasal prominences

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A neonate presents with a failure of the oronasal membrane to rupture during the sixth week. Specify the developmental landmark that fails to form as a result.
back:
• Primitive choanae
• Normally allows communication between nasal pits and oral cavity
• Located immediately behind the primary palate

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the biological process that leads to the relocation of the choanae to their definitive adult position.
back:
• Formation of the secondary palate
• Posterior extension of the primitive nasal chambers
• Results in choanae opening at the junction of the nasal cavity and pharynx

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the embryonic origins of the nasal bridge versus the nasal alae (sides of the nose).
back:
• Bridge: Derived from the frontonasal prominence
• Alae: Derived from the lateral nasal prominences
• Tip/Crest: Derived from merged medial nasal prominences

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: State the anatomical origin of the paranasal sinuses and the developmental period when they reach their maximum size.
back:
• Origin: Diverticula of the lateral nasal walls
• Invade: Maxilla, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid bones
• Maturity: Reach maximum size during puberty

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The epithelial cord that forms in the floor of the [___] eventually canalizes to form the duct connecting the conjunctival sac to the inferior meatus of the nose.
back:
• Nasolacrimal groove
• Separates maxillary and lateral nasal prominences
• Forms the nasolacrimal duct and lacrimal sac

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: An infant presents with a rare midline cleft of the nose. This anomaly typically results from the incomplete merging of which paired structures?
back:
• Medial nasal prominences
• Failure to merge at the midline
• Often associated with cognitive impairment or brain midline defects

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Describe the mechanism by which the nasal septum ensures the complete separation of the right and left nasal passages.
back:
• Grows downward from the frontal prominence
• Fuses with the cephalic surface of the secondary palate
• Occurs simultaneously with palatal shelf fusion

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Distinguish between the primitive nasal cavity and the definitive nasal cavity based on their boundaries with the oral cavity.
back:
• Primitive: Separated by oronasal membrane/primary palate
• Definitive: Separated by the secondary (hard and soft) palate
• Landmark: Incisive foramen marks the transition

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Identify the specific germ layer source and regional origin of the olfactory sensory epithelium.
back:
• Surface Ectoderm
• Derived from the nasal (olfactory) placodes
• Located in the roof of the definitive nasal cavity

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The communication established between the primitive nasal cavity and the oral cavity following the rupture of the [___] membrane is known as the primitive choanae.
back:
• Oronasal membrane
• Occurs during the 6th week
• Located immediately posterior to the primary palate
• Later replaced by definitive choanae

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A neonate presents with persistent epiphora (tearing) and a palpable mass at the medial canthus. This suggests a failure in the canalization of the epithelial cord derived from the [___].
back:
• Nasolacrimal groove
• Located between maxillary and lateral nasal prominences
• Connects lacrimal sac to inferior meatus
• Cord detaches from overlying ectoderm before canalization

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the embryonic origin of the four primary skeletal components of the external nose.
back:
• Bridge: Frontonasal prominence
• Crest and Tip: Merged medial nasal prominences
• Alae (Sides): Lateral nasal prominences
• Philtrum: Intermaxillary segment

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the primitive choanae with the definitive choanae regarding their anatomical location and timing of formation.
back:
• Primitive: Behind primary palate; forms after oronasal membrane rupture (Week 6)
• Definitive: Junction of nasal cavity/pharynx; forms after secondary palate fusion (Week 10)

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Describe the developmental origin and the clinical timeline for the paranasal air sinuses.
back:
• Origin: Diverticula from the lateral nasal wall
• Bones involved: Maxilla, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid
• Growth: Reach maximum size during puberty
• Function: Essential for definitive facial shaping

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Local ectodermal thickenings on the frontonasal prominence that invaginate under the influence of the forebrain to form nasal pits are called [___].
back:
• Nasal (olfactory) placodes
• Appear in the 4th week
• Invaginate during the 5th week
• Surrounded by medial and lateral nasal prominences

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A newborn is diagnosed with a rare midline cleft of the upper lip. This specific malformation indicates an embryological failure in the merging of the [___].
back:
• Two medial nasal prominences
• Results from insufficient midline tissue
• Often associated with holoprosencephaly
• Distinct from lateral cleft lip (Maxillary-Medial fusion failure)

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Detail the two mechanical processes that contribute to the deepening of the nasal pits during the sixth week of gestation.
back:
• Proliferation/growth of surrounding nasal prominences
• Penetration of pits into underlying mesenchyme
• Results in formation of primitive nasal chambers
• Chambers initially separated from oral cavity by oronasal membrane

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Distinguish between the facial derivatives of the medial nasal prominence and the lateral nasal prominence.
back:
• Medial: Philtrum, crest/tip of nose, primary palate, and upper incisors
• Lateral: Alae (wings) of the nose
• Only the medial prominence participates in upper lip formation

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Identify the three components that comprise the intermaxillary segment formed by the merging of the medial nasal prominences.
back:
• Labial: Philtrum of the upper lip
• Upper Jaw: Four incisor teeth
• Palatal: Triangular primary palate
• Segment is continuous with the rostral nasal septum

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Localized thickenings of the surface ectoderm on the frontonasal prominence that invaginate to form the nasal pits are known as [___].
back:
* Nasal (olfactory) placodes
* Formed under the inductive influence of the forebrain
* Develop during the fifth week of gestation

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: A neonate is born with a rare cleft in the exact midline of the upper lip. Name the developmental failure responsible for this condition.
back:
* Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
* Indicates a significant loss of midline tissue
* Often associated with holoprosencephaly and cognitive impairment

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the biological process by which the paranasal air sinuses are formed.
back:
* Develop as diverticula of the lateral nasal wall
* Invade the maxillary, ethmoid, frontal, and sphenoid bones
* Reach maximum size during puberty, contributing to adult facial shape

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the embryonic failure in a child with a simple midline cleft lip versus one presenting with an oblique facial cleft.
back:
* Midline Cleft: Failure of the two medial nasal prominences to merge
* Oblique Cleft: Maxillary prominence fails to merge with the lateral nasal prominence
* Oblique Cleft: Results in an exposed nasolacrimal duct

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Describe the signaling step involving Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) that ensures the separation of the single eye field into two optic primordia.
back:
* SHH is secreted by the prechordal plate
* Upregulates PAX2 in the midline
* Downregulates PAX6 to restrict eye development to lateral regions

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: The structure that temporarily separates the deepening nasal pits from the primitive oral cavity is the [___].
back:
* Oronasal membrane
* Breaks down to allow communication through primitive choanae
* Located immediately behind the primary palate

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: An infant presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye to the upper lip. Identify the anatomical landmark normally formed at this site.
back:
* Nasolacrimal groove
* Separates the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences
* Ectoderm in its floor normally forms the nasolacrimal duct

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Explain the mechanism of choanal repositioning from the primitive state to the definitive choanae.
back:
* Primitive choanae lie behind the primary palate after oronasal membrane rupture
* Secondary palate formation extends the nasal cavity posteriorly
* Definitive choanae eventually reside at the junction of the nasal cavity and pharynx

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Contrast the specific components of the adult nose derived from the medial nasal prominences versus the lateral nasal prominences.
back:
* Medial Nasal: Forms the crest and tip of the nose
* Lateral Nasal: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose
* Both arise during the fifth week as pits deepen

category: Describe the development of nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses
front: Identify the adult nasal structure derived specifically from the frontonasal prominence.
back:
* Bridge of the nose
* Also contributes to the rostral portion of the nasal septum
* Forms the upper border of the stomodeum

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: The failure of the [___] neuropore to close at the end of the fourth week results in cranioschisis, leaving the brain tissue exposed to amniotic fluid.
back: • Cranial neuropore • Leads to anencephaly and brain degeneration • The vault of the skull fails to form completely • Incompatible with long-term survival

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with micrognathia, a posteriorly displaced tongue, and a cleft palate. Identify the primary developmental defect responsible for this sequential presentation.
back: • Primary defect is mandibular hypoplasia (micrognathia) • Prevents the tongue from descending out of the way of palatal shelves • Results in a failure of secondary palate fusion • Collectively known as Robin sequence

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain the embryological basis of hypocalcemia and recurrent infections in a patient with 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge) syndrome.
back: • Failure of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches to differentiate • Results in thymic aplasia or hypoplasia (T-cell deficiency) • Causes parathyroid hypoplasia, leading to low calcium • Linked to abnormal neural crest cell migration

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast a thyroglossal duct cyst with a lateral cervical (branchial) cyst regarding their anatomical midline orientation and embryonic origins.
back: • Thyroglossal: Midline location, moves with tongue protrusion; remnant of thyroid migratory path • Branchial: Lateral location anterior to sternocleidomastoid; remnant of the cervical sinus • Thyroglossal cysts are typically infrahyoid

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Relate the failure of the choroid fissure to close during the seventh week of gestation to its typical clinical manifestation in the iris.
back: • Results in Coloboma iridis (iris cleft) • Caused by incomplete fusion of the optic cup margins • Can extend into the ciliary body or optic nerve • Often presents as a 'keyhole' pupil

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: In the condition known as [___], the tongue remains anchored to the floor of the mouth because the lingual frenulum failed to undergo normal cell degeneration.
back: • Ankyloglossia (Tongue-tie) • Frenulum may extend to the tip of the tongue • Impairs speech and mechanical movement • Results from incomplete separation of the tongue from the jaw

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A child presents with malar hypoplasia, mandibular underdevelopment, and down-slanting palpebral fissures. Associate these findings with the affected embryonic cell population.
back: • Treacher Collins syndrome (mandibulofacial dysostosis) • Caused by deficient neural crest cell proliferation • Affects first and second pharyngeal arch derivatives • Often involves middle ear ossicle malformations

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
