front: Detail the embryological failure responsible for the development of a median (midline) cleft lip and its association with brain malformations.
back: • Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences • Caused by a significant loss of midline tissue • Frequently associated with holoprosencephaly (fused ventricles) • Often involves cognitive impairment and structural brain defects

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish the developmental timing and cause of congenital cataracts associated with maternal Rubella infection.
back: • Rubella infection between weeks 4 and 7 of gestation • Virus crosses placenta to trigger lens opacity • After week 7, the lens is usually safe • Later infections may cause cochlear damage instead

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Identify the specific pharyngeal arch growth failure that allows a cervical sinus to remain in contact with the skin via a branchial fistula.
back: • Second pharyngeal arch fails to grow caudally • Fails to overlap the third and fourth arches • Pharyngeal clefts 2, 3, and 4 remain exposed • Fistula typically opens along the sternocleidomastoid muscle

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: The failure of the cranial neuropore to close results in [___], a lethal condition where the brain tissue is exposed to amniotic fluid and degenerates.
back:
Anencephaly (Cranioschisis)
• Caused by failed closure of the cranial neuropore
• Results in brain degeneration due to amniotic fluid exposure
• Associated with failure of the cranial vault to form.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with excessive salivation, coughing during feeds, and polyhydramnios noted in the maternal history. Identify the likely embryological defect and its primary cause.
back:
Tracheoesophageal Fistula (TEF)
• Abnormality in partitioning of the foregut
• Failure of the tracheoesophageal septum to develop properly
• Often associated with esophageal atresia and VACTERL association.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain how a deletion in the 22q11.2 region leads to the immunological and calcium-related deficits seen in DiGeorge Syndrome.
back:
• Disruption of neural crest cell migration into pharyngeal pouches 3 and 4
• Failure of thymus development (T-cell deficiency)
• Failure of parathyroid gland development (Hypocalcemia and seizures).

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast anterior and posterior cleft deformities based on their anatomical landmark and embryological origins.
back:
• Landmark: Incisive foramen
• Anterior: Failed fusion of maxillary prominence with medial nasal prominence (e.g., cleft lip)
• Posterior: Failed fusion of palatine shelves (e.g., cleft palate).

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Identify the embryological failure responsible for a cleft in the iris, and list three other structures that may be affected if the defect extends posteriorly.
back:
• Failure of the choroid fissure to close (7th week)
• Ciliary body
• Retina and Choroid
• Optic nerve.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A midline swelling in the neck that moves with swallowing and is located near the hyoid bone is most likely a [___].
back:
Thyroglossal Duct Cyst
• Remnant of the migratory pathway of the thyroid gland
• Always located near the midline
• Often associated with a thyroglossal fistula.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a triad of micrognathia, a posteriorly placed tongue (glossoptosis), and a cleft palate. Name this clinical sequence.
back:
Robin Sequence
• Primary defect: Poor growth of the mandible (first arch)
• Posterior tongue prevents palatal shelf fusion
• Can be caused by genetic or environmental factors (e.g., oligohydramnios).

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain the embryological basis of congenital conductive hearing loss involving the stapes.
back:
• Stapes ankylosis (fixation)
• Defective neural crest cell signaling during footplate and oval window development
• Disruption in the transmission of sound vibrations through the ossicle chain.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Differentiate between a lateral branchial fistula and a thyroglossal fistula based on their typical location in the neck.
back:
• Branchial Fistula: Lateral aspect of neck, anterior to sternocleidomastoid muscle
• Thyroglossal Fistula: Midline of the neck, usually near the hyoid bone.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Name the brain malformation frequently associated with midline facial defects like synophthalmia (fused eyes) and describe its early developmental cause.
back:
Holoprosencephaly
• Loss of midline tissue at days 19 to 21 of gestation
• Failure of forebrain separation into two hemispheres
• Associated with SHH mutations or maternal alcohol use.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: The midline neck mass resulting from the failure of the epithelial tract to obliterate following the descent of the thyroid gland is known as a [___].
back:
• Thyroglossal duct cyst
• Often located near the hyoid bone
• Moves upward with tongue protrusion
• May form a fistula if the cyst ruptures

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with tetralogy of Fallot, low-set ears, and facial dysmorphology. Laboratory tests reveal severe hypocalcemia and absent T-cell function. Identify the likely diagnosis and the specific embryological structures involved.
back:
• DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion)
• Maldevelopment of 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches
• Causes thymic aplasia and hypoparathyroidism
• Disruption of neural crest-endoderm interactions

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain the role of neural crest cells in the pathogenesis of Treacher Collins syndrome.
back:
• Failure of crest cell proliferation/survival
• Mutation in TCOF1 (treacle protein)
• Causes apoptosis in first pharyngeal arch populations
• Results in malar and mandibular hypoplasia

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the developmental failure involved in a lateral cleft lip versus an isolated cleft of the secondary palate.
back:
• Lateral Cleft Lip: Maxillary prominence fails to fuse with medial nasal prominence
• Secondary Palate Cleft: Palatine shelves fail to fuse in the midline
• Landmark: Incisive foramen separates anterior and posterior defects

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Discuss the clinical utility of administering glucocorticoids to a mother in premature labor regarding the prevention of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).
back:
• Induces Type II alveolar cell maturation
• Increases surfactant (phospholipid) production
• Lowers surface tension at air-blood interface
• Prevents alveolar collapse (atelectasis) during expiration

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A cleft in the lower portion of the iris, which may extend into the ciliary body or optic nerve, occurs due to the failure of the [___] to close.
back:
• Choroid fissure (retinal fissure)
• Occurs during the 7th week of development
• Known as Coloboma iridis
• Often associated with PAX2 mutations

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with a triad of micrognathia, glossoptosis, and a U-shaped secondary cleft palate. Relate the small mandible to the failure of palatal fusion in this condition.
back:
• Robin Sequence
• Primary defect: Mandibular hypoplasia
• Glossoptosis: Tongue is pushed superiorly/posteriorly
• Mechanical obstruction: Tongue prevents palatine shelves from meeting

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Detail the embryological failure that results in the formation of a lateral cervical cyst located anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
• Persistence of the cervical sinus
• 2nd pharyngeal arch fails to grow over 3rd/4th arches
• Entrapped ectodermal remnants form a cyst or fistula
• Differentials: Midline thyroglossal cysts

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the physiological roles of Type I and Type II alveolar epithelial cells in the neonatal lung.
back:
• Type I: Thin squamous cells for gas exchange
• Type II: Secretory cells producing surfactant
• Surface Tension: Type II cells reduce tension to keep Type I regions patent

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Identify the embryological basis of ankyloglossia (tongue-tie).
back:
• Incomplete cell degeneration
• Lingual frenulum fails to recede normally
• Anchors tongue tip to the floor of the mouth
• Affects speech and breastfeeding

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origins of Laryngeal Structures
front: The internal lining of the larynx is derived from [___], while its cartilages and muscles originate from mesenchyme of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
back:
*   Germ layer: Endoderm
*   Provides: Epithelial lining and mucosal glands
*   Contrast: Cartilages/muscles arise from mesoderm/neural crest

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate presents with significant respiratory distress and a weak cry. Laryngoscopy reveals a membranous septum obstructing the airway at the level of the vocal cords. Name the embryological failure.
back:
*   Condition: Laryngeal Web (or Atresia)
*   Pathophysiology: Failure of laryngeal recanalization during the 10th week
*   Clinical: Leads to airway obstruction and aphonia

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the role of the laryngeal ventricles in the formation of the vocal apparatus.
back:
*   Origin: Formed by vacuolization and recanalization of the laryngeal lumen
*   Differentiation: Folds bounding these lateral recesses become the false and true vocal cords

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the laryngeal derivatives of the 4th pharyngeal arch with those of the 6th pharyngeal arch regarding innervation and musculature.
back:
*   4th Arch: Superior laryngeal nerve; Cricothyroid, levator veli palatini, pharyngeal constrictors
*   6th Arch: Recurrent laryngeal nerve; All intrinsic muscles of larynx (except cricothyroid)

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the pharyngeal swelling responsible for the development of the epiglottis.
back:
*   Structure: Epiglottal swelling
*   Origin: Posterior portion of the 4th pharyngeal arch
*   Location: Situated cranially to the laryngeal orifice

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: As a result of rapid mesenchymal proliferation in the 4th and 6th arches, the laryngeal orifice changes from a sagittal slit into a [___] shape.
back:
*   Shape: T-shaped opening
*   Mechanism: Proliferation of arytenoid swellings toward the tongue
*   Timeline: Occurs during early laryngeal morphogenesis

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A patient undergoing neck surgery suffers damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Which pharyngeal arch cartilage derivatives are anatomically associated with the muscles paralyzed by this injury?
back:
*   Arch: 6th Pharyngeal Arch
*   Associated Cartilages: Cricoid, arytenoid, corniculate, and cuneiform
*   Result: Paralysis of intrinsic laryngeal muscles

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: How is the laryngeal lumen temporarily occluded and subsequently restored during development?
back:
*   Occlusion: Rapid proliferation of laryngeal epithelium
*   Restoration: Vacuolization and recanalization during the 10th week
*   Outcome: Establishes the definitive laryngeal airway

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the skeletal origins of the thyroid cartilage and the epiglottic cartilage.
back:
*   Thyroid Cartilage: 4th pharyngeal arch mesenchyme
*   Epiglottic Cartilage: 4th pharyngeal arch (epiglottal swelling)
*   Note: Both are 4th arch, but epiglottis is a distinct median swelling

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: List the laryngeal cartilages that arise specifically from the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
back:
*   Thyroid cartilage
*   Cricoid cartilage
*   Arytenoid cartilage
*   Corniculate and Cuneiform cartilages

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Embryological Germ Layer Origin of Larynx
front: The internal lining of the larynx is derived from [___], whereas its cartilaginous and muscular components originate from pharyngeal arch mesenchyme.
back:
• Endoderm (internal lining)
• Fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches (cartilages and muscles)
• Mesoderm provides the connective tissue framework.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate presents with an inspiratory stridor and a weak cry. Endoscopy reveals a thin membrane partially obstructing the laryngeal lumen. This condition results from an error in [___].
back:
• Recanalization
• Proliferation of laryngeal epithelium normally occludes the lumen temporarily
• Failure of subsequent vacuolization leads to laryngeal webs or atresia.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the role of pharyngeal arch mesenchyme in transforming the appearance of the laryngeal orifice during the sixth week.
back:
• Rapid proliferation of 4th and 6th arch mesenchyme
• Converts the initial sagittal slit into a T-shaped opening
• Establishes the primitive boundaries of the glottis.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Laryngeal Nerve Supply and Arch Derivation
front: Contrast the innervation of laryngeal muscles derived from the fourth pharyngeal arch with those derived from the sixth pharyngeal arch.
back:
• 4th Arch: Superior laryngeal nerve (branch of CN X)
• 6th Arch: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (branch of CN X)
• All laryngeal muscles are vagal derivatives.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the specific pharyngeal arch cartilages that fuse to form the thyroid, cricoid, and arytenoid structures.
back:
• Fourth pharyngeal arch
• Sixth pharyngeal arch
• These mesenchymal condensations also form corniculate and cuneiform cartilages.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The lateral recesses formed during laryngeal recanalization, which are bounded by tissue folds that differentiate into the vocal cords, are known as [___].
back:
• Laryngeal ventricles
• These recesses define the true and false vocal cords
• Formation occurs after the temporary epithelial occlusion.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Clinical Anatomy of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve
front: A patient undergoing neck surgery suffers damage to the nerve supplying the 4th pharyngeal arch. Which specific laryngeal muscle is most likely paralyzed?
back:
• Cricothyroid muscle
• Supplied by the superior laryngeal nerve
• This muscle is the only laryngeal muscle not supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the mechanism by which the laryngeal lumen becomes patent after the initial period of epithelial proliferation.
back:
• Epithelial cells proliferate and occlude the lumen
• Vacuolization occurs within the epithelial mass
• Recanalization restores patency and forms laryngeal ventricles.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the embryonic origin of the epiglottis with that of the lower laryngeal cartilages.
back:
• Epiglottis: Derived from the hypobranchial eminence (posterior 4th arch)
• Other cartilages: Derived from fused 4th and 6th arch mesenchyme
• Epiglottic swelling marks the cranial boundary of the laryngeal orifice.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Name the transcription factor induced by retinoic acid that is essential for the initial appearance of the respiratory diverticulum.
back:
• TBX4
• Expressed in the endoderm of the gut tube
• Induces the formation and continued growth of the lung bud.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ layer origins of laryngeal structures
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is derived from [___], whereas the cartilages and muscles originate from pharyngeal arch mesenchyme.
back:
* Endoderm
* Provides the lining for the entire respiratory tract
* Connective tissue components arise from splanchnic mesoderm

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A newborn presents with respiratory distress and an audible stridor. Endoscopy reveals a partial occlusion of the laryngeal lumen by a thin tissue sheet. This condition is most likely a failure of which developmental process?
back:
* Recanalization
* Occurs after temporary epithelial proliferation
* Failure results in laryngeal webs or atresia

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the morphologic transition of the laryngeal orifice from a sagittal slit to its characteristic adult appearance.
back:
* Mesenchymal proliferation of the 4th and 6th arches
* Arytenoid swellings enlarge and move medially
* Converts the slit into a T-shaped opening

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Pharyngeal arch derivatives of laryngeal skeleton
front: A 2-day-old infant is diagnosed with a congenital laryngeal anomaly. If the defect involves the cricoid cartilage specifically, the embryological insult likely occurred in the mesenchyme of which pharyngeal arch?
back:
* Sixth pharyngeal arch
* Forms the cricoid, arytenoid, and corniculate cartilages
* The fourth arch primarily forms the thyroid cartilage

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the primary signaling molecule and transcription factor required for the induction of the respiratory diverticulum from the foregut.
back:
* Retinoic Acid (RA)
* TBX4 transcription factor
* RA upregulates TBX4 in the endoderm to initiate budding

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The lateral recesses of the laryngeal cavity, known as laryngeal ventricles, are bounded by tissue folds that eventually differentiate into the [___].
back:
* True and false vocal cords
* Formed during vacuolization and recanalization
* Establish the definitive laryngeal airway

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Following a thyroidectomy, a patient suffers from hoarseness due to injury of the recurrent laryngeal nerve. This nerve provides motor supply to muscles derived from which embryonic structure?
back:
* Sixth pharyngeal arch
* Supplies intrinsic laryngeal muscles
* Excludes the cricothyroid (4th arch/superior laryngeal nerve)

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the developmental relationship between the pharynx and the respiratory primordium before the tracheoesophageal septum is completed.
back:
* Maintain open communication via the laryngeal orifice
* The lung bud is a ventral outgrowth of the foregut
* Separated later by longitudinal tracheoesophageal ridges

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the embryological origin of the epiglottis with that of the thyroid cartilage.
back:
* Epiglottis: Develops from the hypobranchial eminence (posterior 4th arch)
* Thyroid Cartilage: Formed from 4th and 6th arch mesenchyme
* Both are derived from the pharyngeal apparatus

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Name the specific cranial nerve that provides sensory and motor innervation to all laryngeal derivatives of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
* Vagus Nerve (CN X)
* Superior laryngeal branch (4th arch)
* Recurrent laryngeal branch (6th arch)

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origin of Laryngeal Lining
front: The epithelial lining of the internal surface of the larynx is derived from the [___].
back:
• Endoderm.
• Originates from the cranial end of the respiratory diverticulum (lung bud).
• Remains in communication with the pharynx via the laryngeal orifice.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A newborn presents with severe respiratory distress. Examination reveals failed recanalization of the laryngeal lumen during the 10th week of development. Identify the most likely diagnosis.
back:
• Laryngeal atresia.
• Caused by failure of the vacuolization process.
• This follows the period of temporary epithelial occlusion during laryngeal development.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the developmental mechanism that leads to the formation of the laryngeal ventricles and vocal cords.
back:
• Epithelial proliferation: Temporarily occludes the laryngeal lumen.
• Vacuolization/Recanalization: Forms lateral recesses (ventricles).
• Differentiation: Tissue folds bounding these recesses differentiate into true and false vocal cords.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the nerve supply of the cricothyroid muscle with the other intrinsic muscles of the larynx based on their pharyngeal arch origins.
back:
• Cricothyroid: Derived from the 4th arch; supplied by the superior laryngeal nerve (CN X).
• Other Intrinsic Muscles: Derived from the 6th arch; supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the primary reason why the laryngeal orifice changes from a sagittal slit to a T-shaped opening during development.
back:
• Rapid proliferation of mesenchyme.
• Derived from the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
• Transforms the laryngeal inlet into its characteristic adult shape.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: While the laryngeal lining is endodermal, the laryngeal cartilages (thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid) originate from the [___].
back:
• Mesenchyme of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
• Derived specifically from lateral plate mesoderm.
• These cartilaginous components fuse to form the laryngeal framework.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A patient undergoing thyroid surgery suffers injury to the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Which specific pharyngeal arch's muscular derivatives are primarily affected?
back:
• Sixth (6th) pharyngeal arch.
• Affects all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid.
• Clinically results in hoarseness and vocal cord paralysis.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the embryological origin of the epiglottis in relation to the pharyngeal swellings.
back:
• Derived from the hypobranchial eminence.
• Formed specifically by the posterior part of the 4th pharyngeal arch.
• Located immediately behind the tuberculum impar and copula.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the germ layer origins of the laryngeal musculature and the laryngeal epithelium.
back:
• Laryngeal Musculature: Derived from mesoderm (pharyngeal arch mesenchyme).
• Laryngeal Epithelium: Derived from endoderm (respiratory diverticulum).
• Both are integrated into the final laryngeal structure.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the specific transcription factor and molecular trigger required for the initial outgrowth of the respiratory diverticulum from the foregut.
back:
• Transcription factor: TBX4.
• Trigger: Increased Retinoic Acid (RA) from adjacent mesoderm.
• RA upregulates TBX4 in the endoderm to induce laryngeal and lung bud formation.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origin of the Larynx
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is derived from [___], whereas its cartilaginous and muscular components originate from pharyngeal arch mesenchyme.
back:
Endoderm (of the foregut).
- It provides the lining for the larynx, trachea, and bronchi.
- The supporting structures arise from visceral (splanchnic) mesoderm.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A patient presents with persistent hoarseness and vocal cord paralysis following an extensive thyroidectomy. The affected nerve supplies laryngeal muscles derived from which embryological arch?
back:
Sixth Pharyngeal Arch.
- The recurrent laryngeal nerve (branch of CN X) supplies the intrinsic muscles of the larynx.
- These muscles originate from the 6th arch mesenchyme.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the biological mechanism responsible for the formation of the laryngeal ventricles and vocal cords.
back:
Epithelial Recanalization:
- Rapid epithelial proliferation temporarily occludes the laryngeal lumen.
- Vacuolization and recanalization then occur.
- Lateral recesses (ventricles) form, bounded by tissue that differentiates into true and false vocal cords.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the motor innervation of the laryngeal cricothyroid muscle with that of the remaining intrinsic muscles of the larynx based on their arch of origin.
back:
Differentiation by Arch:
- Cricothyroid: Derived from the 4th arch; supplied by the Superior Laryngeal Nerve (CN X).
- Other Intrinsic Muscles: Derived from the 6th arch; supplied by the Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve (CN X).

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the morphological transformation of the laryngeal orifice from early development to the adult state.
back:
Orifice Remodeling:
- Initial state: A simple sagittal slit.
- Transition: Rapid mesenchymal proliferation in arches 4 and 6 creates a T-shaped opening.
- Final state: Acquisition of characteristic adult shape as arch cartilages mature.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Development of the respiratory diverticulum, the precursor to the larynx, is dependent on the upregulation of the transcription factor [___] in the foregut endoderm.
back:
TBX4.
- Induced by increased retinoic acid from adjacent mesoderm.
- Essential for the formation of the lung bud and continued pulmonary differentiation.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate exhibits high-pitched inspiratory stridor. Endoscopy reveals a thin, membranous obstruction partially blocking the airway at the level of the vocal folds. Identify the developmental error.
back:
Incomplete Laryngeal Recanalization.
- Leads to a laryngeal web.
- Caused by a failure of the vacuoles to fully clear the temporary epithelial occlusion during the 10th week.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain how the mesenchyme of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches contributes to the skeletal framework of the neck.
back:
Cartilaginous Derivatives:
- Mesenchyme in these arches chondrifies to form the thyroid, cricoid, and arytenoid cartilages.
- Includes the smaller corniculate and cuneiform cartilages.
- These provide structural rigidity to the upper airway.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the tissue origins of the epiglottis and the cartilaginous derivatives of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
Anatomic Origins:
- 4th and 6th Arch Cartilages: Develop from mesenchyme of the arches.
- Epiglottis: Develops from the epiglottal swelling, a median projection of the posterior part of the 4th arch.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the primary structure that maintains communication between the developing pharynx and the respiratory primordium.
back:
Laryngeal Orifice.
- It connects the foregut (pharynx) to the respiratory diverticulum.
- It is situated between the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Unlike lateral cervical cysts derived from the cervical sinus, a thyroglossal duct cyst is characteristically found in the [___] of the neck, near the hyoid bone.
back:
* Midline of the neck
* Remnant of the thyroid's migratory pathway
* Typically moves upward during swallowing or tongue protrusion

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A neonate presents with a triad of micrognathia, glossoptosis, and a secondary cleft palate. Identify this clinical sequence and its primary developmental defect.
back:
* Robin Sequence
* Primary defect: Mandibular hypoplasia (poor growth of 1st arch)
* Pathogenesis: Posteriorly placed tongue prevents palatal shelf fusion

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain how mutations in the TCOF1 gene lead to the facial features seen in Treacher Collins syndrome.
back:
* Encodes 'treacle' protein
* Deficiency leads to neural crest cell apoptosis
* Results in hypoplasia of the maxilla, mandible, and zygomatic arches

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the clinical presentation of isolated esophageal atresia with a pure H-type tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF).
back:
* Isolated Atresia: Excessive drooling, inability to pass a tube, no abdominal air
* H-type TEF: Recurrent coughing/cyanosis during feeding, abdominal distention (air in gut)

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Identify the genetic mutation and the hallmark facial feature associated with Van der Woude syndrome.
back:
* IRF6 (Interferon Regulatory Factor 6) mutation
* Pits in the lower lip
* Most common syndrome associated with cleft lip/palate

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: In [___], the tongue is not freed from the floor of the mouth because the lingual frenulum remains attached to the tip of the tongue.
back:
* Ankyloglossia (Tongue-tie)
* Failure of cell degeneration in the floor of the mouth
* Affects speech and tongue mobility

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A newborn presents with synophthalmia and a single telencephalic vesicle. Which signaling molecule’s deficiency at the prechordal plate is responsible for this midline defect?
back:
* Sonic Hedgehog (SHH)
* Failure to separate the single eye field into two primordia
* Leads to holoprosencephaly spectrum

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Distinguish between the embryological origins of preauricular pits and preauricular skin tags.
back:
* Pits: Failure of 1st arch tissue invagination to form the external meatus
* Tags: Accessory/duplicated tissue growth from the auricular hillocks
* Both often suggest concurrent renal or cardiac defects

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the effects of maternal rubella infection on fetal ear and eye development based on the timing of infection.
back:
* 4–7 weeks: Congenital cataracts (lens damage)
* >7 weeks: Sensorineural hearing loss (cochlear abnormalities)
* Earlier infections typically cause more severe multisystem defects

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Name the specific embryological structure that fails to fuse in a patient presenting with coloboma iridis.
back:
* Choroid fissure (Optic fissure)
* Fusion normally occurs during the 7th week
* Cleft may extend from the iris to the optic nerve

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: In the condition [___], the tongue is not freed from the floor of the mouth because the frenulum extends to the tip of the tongue.
back:
• Ankyloglossia
• Commonly referred to as tongue-tie
• Results from failure of normal cell degeneration in the lingual frenulum area

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A neonate with persistent truncus arteriosus presents with hypocalcemic seizures and an absent T-cell response. This condition results from the developmental failure of the [___] and [___] pharyngeal pouches.
back:
• 3rd pharyngeal pouch (Inferior parathyroids and thymus)
• 4th pharyngeal pouch (Superior parathyroids)
• Diagnosis: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome (DiGeorge Syndrome)

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Explain the embryological failure that results in an external branchial fistula located anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
back:
• 2nd pharyngeal arch fails to grow caudally over the 3rd and 4th arches
• Failure to obliterate the cervical sinus
• Remnants of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th pharyngeal clefts persist

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the embryological fusion failures seen in anterior versus posterior cleft deformities using the incisive foramen as the landmark.
back:
• Anterior Clefts: Failure of maxillary prominence to fuse with medial nasal prominence (e.g., cleft lip)
• Posterior Clefts: Failure of palatine shelves to fuse with each other or the nasal septum (e.g., cleft secondary palate)

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Mention the specific associated congenital anomalies grouped under the VACTERL association often identified in infants with tracheoesophageal fistulas.
back:
• Vertebral, Anal, Cardiac
• Tracheoesophageal fistula, Esophageal atresia
• Renal and Limb defects
• Occurs more frequently than predicted by chance

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A child with flat maxillary and zygomatic bones presents with preauricular skin tags and vertebral defects (fused vertebrae). This clinical spectrum is known as [___].
back:
• Hemifacial Microsomia
• Also known as Goldenhar Syndrome or Oculoauriculovertebral spectrum
• Affects structures derived from 1st and 2nd pharyngeal arches

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: A pediatric patient presents with a mobile, painless midline neck mass located just below the hyoid bone that elevates upon tongue protrusion. Identify the condition.
back:
• Thyroglossal duct cyst
• Remnant of the thyroid migratory pathway from foramen cecum to the neck
• Always located near or in the midline

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Describe the specific developmental failure that leads to a cleft in the iris, known as Coloboma iridis.
back:
• Failure of the choroid fissure (optic fissure) to fuse
• Typically occurs during the 7th week of development
• May extend to the ciliary body, retina, or optic nerve

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Contrast the anatomical causes of Conductive versus Sensorineural hearing loss in neonates.
back:
• Conductive: Defects in external ear canal, eardrum, or ossicles (e.g., stapes fixation)
• Sensorineural: Abnormalities in hair cells, spiral ganglion, or auditory nerve (CN VIII)

category: Give the associated congenital anomalies
front: Identify the key regulatory gene whose mutation is specifically associated with Aniridia (absence of the iris).
back:
• PAX6
• Master regulatory gene for eye development
• Regulates lens induction and optic cup differentiation

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origin of Laryngeal Lining
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is derived from the [___] germ layer of the foregut.
back:
• Endoderm.
• Forms the mucosal lining and laryngeal glands.
• Arises from the respiratory diverticulum (lung bud) appearing at week 4.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate presents with inspiratory stridor and a weak cry. Endoscopy reveals a thin tissue membrane obstructing the laryngeal lumen. Explain the embryological failure.
back:
• Failure of laryngeal recanalization.
• Occurs after a normal period of temporary epithelial proliferation and occlusion.
• Leads to laryngeal webs or, in severe cases, atresia.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which retinoic acid (RA) initiates the formation of the laryngeal primordium.
back:
• RA increases in the adjacent splanchnic mesoderm.
• RA upregulates the transcription factor TBX4 in the foregut endoderm.
• TBX4 induces the outgrowth of the respiratory diverticulum.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the motor innervation of the cricothyroid muscle with the intrinsic muscles of the larynx based on their pharyngeal arch origins.
back:
• Cricothyroid: Derived from 4th arch; supplied by Superior Laryngeal Nerve (CN X).
• Intrinsic Muscles: Derived from 6th arch; supplied by Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve (CN X).

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the developmental process that creates the laryngeal ventricles and the subsequent vocal folds.
back:
• Vacuolization and recanalization of the occluded epithelial lumen.
• Lateral recesses form laryngeal ventricles.
• Surrounding tissue folds differentiate into true and false vocal cords.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The laryngeal cartilages, such as the thyroid and cricoid, are derived from the mesenchyme of the [___] pharyngeal arches.
back:
• 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
• Specifically derived from lateral plate mesoderm.
• Includes thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid, corniculate, and cuneiform cartilages.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: During the 6th week, the laryngeal orifice changes from a sagittal slit to a T-shaped opening. What causes this morphologic transformation?
back:
• Rapid proliferation of mesenchyme from the 4th and 6th arches.
• Formation of the arytenoid swellings.
• Conversion of the simple slit into the characteristic adult shape.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the embryological origin of the epiglottis.
back:
• Develops from the epiglottal swelling.
• Derived from the posterior portion of the 4th pharyngeal arch.
• Located cranial to the laryngeal orifice.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish the embryonic tissue origins of the laryngeal muscles from those of the laryngeal cartilages.
back:
• Muscles: Derived from the mesoderm of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
• Cartilages: Derived from the lateral plate mesoderm within these same arches.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the landmark that maintains communication between the developing respiratory primordium and the pharynx.
back:
• Laryngeal orifice (laryngotracheal orifice).
• Located at the site of the original diverticulum outgrowth.
• Bounded by arytenoid swellings and the epiglottis.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is entirely derived from the embryonic [___].
back:
● Endoderm
● Specifically originates from the cranial end of the respiratory diverticulum (lung bud).
● The diverticulum arises from the ventral wall of the foregut during the fourth week.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve and 6th Arch Derivatives
front: A neonate presents with a hoarse cry following corrective surgery for a patent ductus arteriosus. The nerve likely injured innervates laryngeal muscles derived from which pharyngeal arch?
back:
● Sixth Pharyngeal Arch
● The recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X branch) is often injured.
● It supplies the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (except cricothyroid) which develop from 6th arch mesenchyme.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Laryngeal Recanalization and Vocal Cord Formation
front: Describe the embryological process that restores the laryngeal lumen following its temporary occlusion by proliferating epithelium.
back:
● Vacuolization and Recanalization
● Occurs around the 10th week of development.
● This process creates lateral recesses called laryngeal ventricles, which are bounded by the true and false vocal cords.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Pharyngeal Arch Innervation of Laryngeal Musculature
front: Contrast the motor innervation of the cricothyroid muscle with the other intrinsic muscles of the larynx based on their pharyngeal arch origins.
back:
● Cricothyroid (4th Arch): Supplied by the superior laryngeal nerve.
● Other Intrinsic Muscles (6th Arch): Supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
● Both nerves are branches of the Vagus nerve (CN X).

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Morphological Development of the Laryngeal Orifice
front: As a result of rapid mesenchymal proliferation in the 4th and 6th arches, the laryngeal orifice changes from a sagittal slit to what specific shape?
back:
● T-shaped Opening
● Caused by the expansion of the arytenoid swellings.
● As the mesenchyme transforms into definitive cartilages, the orifice assumes the characteristic adult laryngeal shape.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Skeletal Derivatives of the 4th and 6th Arches
front: The thyroid, cricoid, and [___] cartilages represent the primary skeletal derivatives formed by the fusion of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arch mesenchyme.
back:
● Arytenoid Cartilages
● Also includes the corniculate and cuneiform cartilages.
● These structures provide the rigid framework for the laryngeal airway.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A newborn presents with respiratory stridor; laryngoscopy reveals a thin tissue membrane obstructing the airway at the level of the vocal cords. Name the developmental error.
back:
● Incomplete Laryngeal Recanalization
● Leads to the formation of laryngeal webs or stenosis.
● Complete failure of this process results in laryngeal atresia.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain how the respiratory primordium maintains communication with the pharynx during the formation of the tracheoesophageal septum.
back:
● Via the Laryngeal Orifice
● While the septum separates the trachea from the esophagus, the cranial-most portion remains open.
● This ensures the pharynx and larynx remain continuous for air passage.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the embryonic tissue origins of the laryngeal cartilages versus the skeletal elements of the first pharyngeal arch.
back:
● Larynx (4th/6th Arches): Derived from lateral plate (splanchnic) mesoderm.
● First Arch Skeletal Elements: Derived from neural crest cells (Viscerocranium).
● Both contribute to the functional head and neck apparatus.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the specific median swelling, derived from the posterior part of the fourth arch, that forms the epiglottis.
back:
● Epiglottal Swelling
● Also referred to as the hypobranchial eminence.
● It marks the upper boundary of the T-shaped laryngeal orifice.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The internal lining of the larynx is entirely derived from [___], while its cartilages and muscles originate from the mesenchyme of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
• Endoderm
• Specifically, it arises from the endodermal lining of the cranial end of the respiratory diverticulum.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A newborn presents with high-pitched inspiratory stridor. Laryngoscopy shows a thin membrane partially occluding the glottis, resulting from incomplete vacuolization of the laryngeal lumen. Identify the condition.
back:
• Laryngeal Web
• Occurs due to failed or partial recanalization of the larynx during the tenth week of development.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the role of mesenchyme proliferation from the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches in changing the morphology of the primitive laryngeal orifice.
back:
• Converts the initial sagittal slit-like opening into a T-shaped orifice.
• Further remodeling by arytenoid swellings eventually establishes the characteristic adult laryngeal shape.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the embryological arch origin and nerve supply of the cricothyroid muscle with the other intrinsic muscles of the larynx.
back:
• Cricothyroid: Derived from the 4th arch; supplied by the superior laryngeal nerve.
• Other Intrinsic Muscles: Derived from the 6th arch; supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the developmental process that creates the laryngeal ventricles and separates the false from the true vocal cords.
back:
• Recanalization following temporary epithelial occlusion.
• Vacuolization of the proliferated laryngeal epithelium forms lateral recesses (ventricles) bounded by tissue folds.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The [___] cartilages, along with the thyroid and cricoid cartilages, are formed by the fusion of cartilaginous components from the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
• Arytenoid, corniculate, and cuneiform
• These are the skeletal derivatives of the laryngeal mesenchyme.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A surgeon performing a thyroidectomy must identify the recurrent laryngeal nerve. This nerve innervates muscles derived from which specific pharyngeal arch?
back:
• Sixth pharyngeal arch
• This arch gives rise to the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (excluding the cricothyroid).

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the mechanism by which the laryngeal lumen is restored after the temporary period of epithelial proliferation.
back:
• Vacuolization: Small spaces form within the solid epithelial plug.
• Recanalization: These spaces coalesce to reopen the airway lumen, typically by the tenth week.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the developmental origin of the epiglottis and the thyroid cartilage.
back:
• Epiglottis: Derived from the hypobranchial eminence (posterior part of the 4th pharyngeal arch).
• Thyroid Cartilage: Derived from the fused cartilaginous bars of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Name the cranial nerve that provides all motor and sensory innervation to the laryngeal derivatives of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
• Vagus Nerve (Cranial Nerve X)
• Branching into the superior laryngeal and recurrent laryngeal nerves to supply respective arch derivatives.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is derived from [___].
back:
• Endoderm of the foregut.
• Specifically, the cranial end of the laryngotracheal tube.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate presents with a high-pitched cry and respiratory distress. Examination reveals a thin membrane partially obstructing the laryngeal lumen. Identify the embryological error.
back:
• Laryngeal Web.
• Caused by incomplete recanalization of the laryngeal lumen during the 10th week of development.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain the role of vacuolization and recanalization in the development of laryngeal ventricles.
back:
• Epithelial proliferation initially occludes the laryngeal lumen.
• Vacuolization during the 10th week recanalizes the airway.
• This process leaves lateral recesses (ventricles) bounded by folds that become vocal cords.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Contrast the innervation of laryngeal muscles derived from the fourth pharyngeal arch with those from the sixth arch.
back:
• Fourth Arch: Innervated by the Superior Laryngeal Nerve (supplies Cricothyroid).
• Sixth Arch: Innervated by the Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve (supplies all other intrinsic muscles).

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: List the laryngeal cartilages derived from the mesenchyme of the fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.
back:
• Thyroid cartilage.
• Cricoid cartilage.
• Arytenoid, Corniculate, and Cuneiform cartilages.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Proliferation of the fourth and sixth arch mesenchyme transforms the sagittal slit laryngeal orifice into a [___] shape.
back:
• T-shaped.
• This occurs as the mesenchyme rapidly expands to form the primitive glottis.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Following a thyroidectomy, a patient experiences significant hoarseness and a weak voice. Damage to a branch of the Vagus nerve supplying the 6th arch is suspected. Identify the nerve.
back:
• Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve.
• It supplies the intrinsic muscles of the larynx (excluding cricothyroid) and provides sensory supply below the vocal folds.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Detail the embryological origin of the epiglottis.
back:
• Derived from the hypobranchial eminence.
• Formed by the proliferation of mesoderm in the 3rd and 4th pharyngeal arches.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the tissue origins of the laryngeal epithelium and its supporting cartilaginous framework.
back:
• Epithelium: Derived from Endoderm.
• Cartilages/Muscles: Derived from Splanchnic Mesenchyme of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Identify the primary signaling center and transcription factor responsible for the initial outgrowth of the respiratory diverticulum.
back:
• Signaling Center: Foregut endoderm.
• Transcription Factor: TBX4 (induced by Retinoic Acid from adjacent mesoderm).

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origin of Laryngeal Epithelium
front: The internal epithelial lining of the larynx is derived from the [___] germ layer, which also forms the rest of the respiratory tract.
back:
• Endoderm.
• Provides the internal lining for the larynx, trachea, bronchi, and lungs.
• The cartilaginous and muscular components originate from mesoderm.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A newborn presents with stridor and respiratory distress. Endoscopy reveals a persistent tissue membrane blocking the laryngeal lumen. This condition most likely results from a failure in which embryological process?
back:
• Recanalization (or Vacuolization).
• The laryngeal lumen is temporarily occluded by epithelial proliferation.
• Failure to vacuolize results in laryngeal webs or atresia.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Explain how the laryngeal orifice transforms from a sagittal slit into its characteristic T-shaped adult configuration.
back:
• Rapid proliferation of 4th and 6th arch mesenchyme.
• Expansion of the arytenoid swellings toward the midline.
• This mesenchymal growth reshapes the initial slit into a T-shaped opening.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Pharyngeal Arch Nerve Supply to Larynx
front: During a surgical procedure, the superior laryngeal nerve is injured. Contrast the resulting laryngeal muscular deficit with an injury involving the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
back:
• Superior Laryngeal Nerve: Loss of cricothyroid muscle (4th arch).
• Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve: Loss of all other intrinsic muscles (6th arch).
• Both nerves are branches of CN X (Vagus).

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Molecular Induction of the Respiratory Bud
front: Identify the primary transcription factor and the inducing signaling molecule responsible for initiating the outgrowth of the laryngeal/respiratory primordium.
back:
• Transcription Factor: TBX4.
• Inducer: Retinoic Acid (RA).
• RA from adjacent mesoderm upregulates TBX4 in the foregut endoderm to induce the lung bud.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: The laryngeal ventricles, bounded by folds that differentiate into true and false vocal cords, appear following the process of [___].
back:
• Recanalization.
• Proliferating epithelium initially occludes the lumen.
• Subsequent vacuolization creates these lateral recesses and defining tissue folds.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: A neonate is born with a tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF). Apply your knowledge of laryngeal development to explain why the laryngeal orifice remains in communication with the pharynx despite this separation.
back:
• The tracheoesophageal septum divides the foregut into the esophagus and trachea.
• The larynx remains open to the pharynx through the laryngeal orifice.
• This ensures a continuous airway from the pharynx to the lungs.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Describe the embryological mechanism that leads to the formation of the arytenoid, cricoid, and thyroid cartilages.
back:
• Mesenchyme of the 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches undergoes rapid proliferation.
• These mesenchymal bars differentiate into the adult laryngeal skeletal framework.
• They replace the primitive arch cartilages via chondrogenesis.

category: Describe the development of larynx
front: Distinguish between the embryological origins of the epiglottis and the main laryngeal cartilages (thyroid/cricoid).
back:
• Epiglottis: Derived from the hypobranchial eminence (posterior 4th arch).
• Thyroid/Cricoid/Arytenoid: Derived from the mesenchymal fusion of 4th and 6th pharyngeal arches.
• Both involve CN X innervation.

category: Describe the development of larynx
coreConcept: Nervous System Integration in Larynx Development
front: Specify the cranial nerve responsible for the motor supply of the larynx and its two major developmental branches.
back:
• Cranial Nerve: Vagus (CN X).
• Superior Laryngeal Nerve: Supplies 4th arch derivatives (cricothyroid).
• Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve: Supplies 6th arch derivatives (intrinsic laryngeal muscles).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The upper lip is formed through the fusion of the two maxillary prominences and the two [___] prominences.
back:
• Medial nasal
• Note: The lateral nasal prominences do not participate in forming the upper lip.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant presents with a cleft in the upper lip that extends into the nose. This defect is embryologically caused by the failure of the [___] prominence to fuse with the [___] prominence.
back:
• Maxillary; Medial nasal
• Occurs due to a partial or complete lack of fusion on one or both sides.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Summarize the formation of the intermaxillary segment and its three primary derivatives.
back:
• Formed by merging the two medial nasal prominences.
• Derivatives: Philtrum of upper lip, four incisor teeth (premaxilla), and triangular primary palate.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological failure leading to a standard cleft lip versus an oblique facial cleft.
back:
• Cleft lip: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominences to fuse.
• Oblique facial cleft: Failure of maxillary prominence to merge with the lateral nasal prominence along the nasolacrimal groove.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the mesenchymal prominences responsible for the formation of the lower lip and lower jaw.
back:
• Mandibular prominences
• These arise from the first pharyngeal arch and merge across the midline.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The labial component of the intermaxillary segment specifically gives rise to the [___] of the upper lip.
back:
• Philtrum
• This is the central indentation of the upper lip formed by the merged medial nasal prominences.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A neonate is born with a rare midline gap in the upper lip. State the specific developmental failure and the associated risk for internal brain anomalies.
back:
• Failure: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
• Risk: Holoprosencephaly (loss of midline brain structures and fused ventricles).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Describe the role of the furrow between the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences in the development of the nasolacrimal system.
back:
• Ectoderm in the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid cord.
• The cord detaches and canalizes to form the nasolacrimal duct.
• The superior end expands to form the lacrimal sac.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish between cleft lip and isolated cleft palate regarding their incidence in different sexes.
back:
• Cleft lip (± cleft palate): More common in males (65%).
• Isolated cleft palate: More common in females (55%).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Name the anatomical landmark that serves as the boundary between the primary and secondary palate.
back:
• Incisive foramen
• It lies in the midline between the triangular primary palate and the fused palatine shelves.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The central portion of the upper lip, known as the philtrum, is derived from the [___] segment, which is formed by the merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
back:
● Intermaxillary segment
● Derived from merged medial nasal prominences
● Formed at a deep level during the sixth week
● Continuous with the rostral nasal septum.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A neonate presents with a unilateral cleft of the upper lip located lateral to the philtrum. This malformation is primarily caused by a failure of fusion between [___].
back:
● Maxillary prominence and medial nasal prominence
● Occurs on one or both sides
● Result of partial or complete fusion failure
● Classified as an anterior cleft deformity.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Explain the role of the first pharyngeal arch prominences in the formation of the definitive upper and lower lips.
back:
● Maxillary prominences: Form lateral parts of upper lip
● Medial nasal prominences: Merge to form the central philtrum
● Mandibular prominences: Merge across midline to form the lower lip and jaw.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological failure leading to a standard lateral cleft lip with that of a rare median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
● Lateral Cleft: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominence fusion
● Median Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
● Median clefts often signal underlying brain defects like holoprosencephaly.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the specific facial prominences that are excluded from the margin of the definitive upper lip despite their proximity to the nose.
back:
● Lateral nasal prominences
● Form the alae (sides) of the nose
● Separated from maxillary prominence by the nasolacrimal groove
● Do not contribute to the lip margin.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The solid epithelial cord that forms in the floor of the groove between the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences eventually canalizes to become the [___].
back:
● Nasolacrimal duct
● Upper end widens to form the lacrimal sac
● Runs from medial eye corner to inferior nasal meatus
● Disruption causes oblique facial clefts.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A child is born with an 'oblique facial cleft' where the nasolacrimal duct is exposed to the surface. This is caused by the failure of the [___] to merge.
back:
● Maxillary prominence and lateral nasal prominence
● Failure to merge along the nasolacrimal groove line
● Results in a cleft extending from the eye to the lip.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Detail the mesenchymal origin of the facial prominences and how it relates to common multi-organ congenital syndromes.
back:
● Derived from neural crest cells
● Neural crest also contributes to the heart and skull
● Insults (e.g., alcohol, retinoic acid) often cause combined facial and cardiac defects.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish the sensory innervation of the upper lip from the lower lip based on their embryological origins.
back:
● Upper Lip: Supplied by Maxillary nerve (V2) via the maxillary process
● Lower Lip: Supplied by Mandibular nerve (V3) via the mandibular process
● Both are branches of the Trigeminal nerve (Arch 1).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Specify the anatomical landmark used to categorize cleft deformities into anterior or posterior types.
back:
● Incisive foramen
● Anterior: Cleft lip, cleft upper jaw (premaxilla)
● Posterior: Cleft secondary palate, cleft uvula
● Reflects different timing and mechanisms of fusion.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two [___] and the two maxillary prominences.
back:
- Medial nasal prominences
- Forms the philtrum and central segment
- Lateral portions arise from maxillary processes
- Failure of this fusion leads to cleft lip

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A newborn presents with a cleft in the upper lip that extends into the nostril on the right side. Identify the embryological failure responsible for this defect.
back:
- Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence
- Occurs on the affected side during the 6th-7th week
- Incisive foramen is the landmark dividing anterior/posterior clefts

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Describe the formation and specific labial component of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
- Formed by the merging of two medial nasal prominences at a deep level
- Labial component forms the philtrum of the upper lip
- Also contains the four incisor teeth and primary palate

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological origins of a median cleft lip versus a standard lateral cleft lip.
back:
- Median Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences in the midline
- Lateral Cleft: Failure of fusion between maxillary and medial nasal prominences
- Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Explain the structural failure leading to an oblique facial cleft and specify which duct is typically exposed.
back:
- Failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with the lateral nasal prominence
- Occurs along the line of the nasolacrimal groove
- Results in the nasolacrimal duct being exposed to the surface

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The lower lip and jaw are formed by the merging of the paired [___] across the midline.
back:
- Mandibular prominences
- Derived from the first pharyngeal arch
- Merging occurs early in the midline
- Innervated by the mandibular nerve (V3)

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant is born with a bilateral cleft lip and distinctive pits on the lower lip. Name the likely syndrome and the associated gene mutation.
back:
- Van der Woude syndrome
- IRF6 (Interferon Regulatory Factor 6) mutation
- Autosomal dominant inheritance
- Most common syndrome associated with cleft lip and palate

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Detail the process by which the nasolacrimal duct is established between facial prominences.
back:
- Ectoderm in the floor of the nasolacrimal groove forms a solid epithelial cord
- Cord detaches from surface ectoderm and canalizes
- Connects the medial corner of the eye to the inferior meatus

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish the sensory innervation of the upper lip from that of the lower lip based on their embryological origins.
back:
- Upper lip: Maxillary nerve (V2) via the maxillary prominence
- Lower lip: Mandibular nerve (V3) via the mandibular prominence
- Both are branches of the Trigeminal nerve (CN V)

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Specify the exact embryological precursor of the philtrum and explain its anatomical significance in midline defects.
back:
- Merged medial nasal prominences (labial component of intermaxillary segment)
- Failure of these prominences to merge results in midline (median) clefts
- Midline defects often suggest underlying forebrain abnormalities

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The [___] of the upper lip is specifically derived from the labial component of the intermaxillary segment.
back:
• Philtrum
  • Formed by the merging of two medial nasal prominences
  • Represents the central part of the definitive upper lip

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A neonate is born with a unilateral gap in the upper lip lateral to the midline. Identify the specific developmental failure involved.
back:
• Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence
  • Occurs on the affected side
  • Commonly involves the primary palate anterior to the incisive foramen

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Explain the role of the maxillary prominences in the formation of the definitive upper lip.
back:
• They grow medially during the 6th and 7th weeks
  • Compress the medial nasal prominences toward the midline
  • Form the lateral portions of the upper lip and the cheeks

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological defects resulting in a unilateral lateral cleft lip versus a median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
• Lateral Cleft: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominence fusion
  • Median Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences
  • Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the mesenchymal prominences responsible for forming the lower lip and jaw.
back:
• Mandibular prominences
  • Derived from the first pharyngeal arch
  • Merge across the midline to form the lower boundary of the stomodeum

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: During facial development, the maxillary prominence is initially separated from the lateral nasal prominence by the [___].
back:
• Nasolacrimal groove
  • Ectoderm in its floor forms the nasolacrimal duct
  • Later obliterated as prominences merge to form the cheek

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant presents with a cleft extending from the medial corner of the eye down to the upper lip, exposing the nasolacrimal duct. State the underlying diagnosis.
back:
• Oblique facial cleft
  • Caused by failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with the lateral nasal prominence
  • The nasolacrimal duct remains open to the surface

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Describe the three morphological components of the intermaxillary segment formed during deep merging of the medial nasal prominences.
back:
• Labial component (forms the philtrum)
  • Upper jaw component (carries the four incisor teeth)
  • Palatal component (forms the triangular primary palate)

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish the contribution of the lateral nasal prominences from the medial nasal prominences in lip and nose formation.
back:
• Medial nasal: Forms philtrum, crest, and tip of the nose
  • Lateral nasal: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose
  • Lateral nasal prominences do not participate in lip formation

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: State the specific embryological timing and tissue origin for the facial prominences.
back:
• Appear at the end of the 4th week
  • Consist primarily of neural crest-derived mesenchyme
  • Formed mainly by the first pair of pharyngeal arches

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The upper lip is embryologically formed by the fusion of the two [___] nasal prominences and the two maxillary prominences.
back:
• Medial
• Maxillary prominences grow medially, compressing these toward the midline.
• This occurs during the sixth and seventh weeks of development.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant is born with a gap in the upper lip extending into the nostril on the right side. Identify the specific embryological failure.
back:
• Failure of fusion between the right maxillary prominence and right medial nasal prominence.
• This is an anterior cleft deformity.
• Occurs due to mesenchymal deficiency or mechanical obstruction.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Explain the role of the intermaxillary segment in the formation of the definitive upper lip.
back:
• Formed by the merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
• Gives rise to the labial component.
• This component forms the philtrum of the upper lip.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological origins of a common lateral cleft lip with the rare median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
• Lateral Cleft: Maxillary prominence fails to fuse with medial nasal prominence.
• Median Cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences.
• Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly and midline brain loss.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the mesenchymal structures that merge across the midline to form the lower lip and jaw.
back:
• Paired mandibular prominences.
• Derived from the first pharyngeal arch.
• These merge early in development to form the lower boundary of the stomodeum.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Failure of the maxillary prominence to merge with its corresponding [___] nasal prominence along the nasolacrimal groove results in an oblique facial cleft.
back:
• Lateral
• This results in the nasolacrimal duct being exposed to the surface.
• Normally, these prominences merge after the duct canalizes.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A newborn presents with a bilateral cleft lip and distinct pits in the lower lip. Name the likely syndrome and the associated gene.
back:
• Van der Woude syndrome.
• IRF6 (Interferon Regulatory Factor 6).
• It is the most common syndrome associated with cleft lip and palate.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Detail the mechanism by which the maxillary prominences contribute to both the lip and the cheek structures.
back:
• Medial growth: Fuses with medial nasal prominences for the lateral upper lip.
• Lateral expansion: Increases in size to form the maxilla and cheeks.
• Derived from neural crest-derived mesenchyme of the first arch.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish between the roles of the medial and lateral nasal prominences in adult nasal/lip anatomy.
back:
• Medial: Forms the philtrum (lip), crest, and tip of the nose.
• Lateral: Forms the alae (sides) of the nose.
• Lateral nasal prominences do NOT participate in upper lip formation.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Which anatomical landmark is used to divide "anterior" from "posterior" cleft deformities of the lip and palate?
back:
• Incisive foramen.
• Anterior clefts: Include lateral cleft lip and primary palate defects.
• Posterior clefts: Include secondary palate and uvula defects.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The central philtrum of the upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two [___].
back:
* Medial nasal prominences
* These merged structures form the intermaxillary segment
* The segment also contributes to the primary palate.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A newborn presents with a cleft in the upper lip extending into the nostril. This defect results from the failure of fusion between which two mesenchymal prominences?
back:
* Maxillary prominence
* Medial nasal prominence
* This is the most common anterior facial cleft deformity.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Explain the role of the mandibular prominences in the formation of the lower lip.
back:
* Derived from the first pharyngeal arch
* Prominences grow medially and merge across the midline
* Forms the lower jaw, lower lip, and associated musculature.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological failure in a common lateral cleft lip versus a rare median cleft lip.
back:
* Lateral Cleft: Maxillary and medial nasal prominences fail to fuse.
* Median Cleft: The two medial nasal prominences fail to merge.
* Median clefts are often associated with holoprosencephaly.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the three distinct anatomical components derived from the intermaxillary segment.
back:
* Labial component (forms the philtrum)
* Upper jaw component (carries the four incisor teeth)
* Palatal component (forms the triangular primary palate).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The [___] separates the maxillary and lateral nasal prominences, eventually canalizing to form a duct connecting the eye to the nose.
back:
* Nasolacrimal groove
* Ectoderm in its floor forms a solid epithelial cord
* Cord canalizes to become the nasolacrimal duct.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant is born with a cleft running from the medial corner of the eye to the lip, exposing the nasolacrimal duct. Merging of which two prominences failed to occur?
back:
* Maxillary prominence
* Lateral nasal prominence
* This results in an oblique facial cleft.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Describe the mechanism by which the maxillary prominences participate in upper lip closure during the 6th and 7th weeks.
back:
* Maxillary prominences increase in size and grow medially
* They compress the medial nasal prominences toward the midline
* Fusion occurs to form the definitive upper lip.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryonic origins of the nasal crest/tip versus the nasal alae (sides).
back:
* Crest and Tip: Formed by the merged medial nasal prominences.
* Alae (Sides): Formed by the lateral nasal prominences.
* Bridge: Formed by the frontonasal prominence.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Mention the diagnostic lower lip feature often found in patients with Van der Woude syndrome.
back:
* Paramedian lower lip pits
* Inherited as autosomal dominant
* Caused by mutations in the IRF6 gene.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
coreConcept: Embryological Components of the Upper Lip
front: The upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two [___] prominences and the two maxillary prominences.
back:
• Medial nasal prominences
• These merge with the maxillary prominences to create a continuous upper lip
• Note: Lateral nasal prominences do not participate in forming the lip.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: An infant presents with a unilateral cleft of the upper lip. Identify the embryological failure that results in this specific defect.
back:
• Failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the medial nasal prominence
• This occurs on one side, typically extending into the nose in severe cases.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Describe the embryological origin of the philtrum of the upper lip.
back:
• Derived from the intermaxillary segment
• This segment is formed by the merging of the two medial nasal prominences in the midline.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Distinguish between the embryological failures leading to a lateral cleft lip versus a median (midline) cleft lip.
back:
• Lateral cleft: Failure of maxillary and medial nasal prominences to fuse.
• Median cleft: Incomplete merging of the two medial nasal prominences in the midline.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Identify the mesenchymal prominences responsible for the formation of the lower lip and jaw.
back:
• Paired mandibular prominences
• These originate from the first pharyngeal arch and merge across the midline early in development.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The [___] serves as the midline anatomical landmark that divides anterior cleft deformities from posterior cleft deformities.
back:
• Incisive foramen
• Clefts anterior to it involve the lip and primary palate
• Clefts posterior involve the secondary palate and uvula.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: A neonate is born with a bilateral cleft lip and distinctive pits on the lower lip. Name the likely syndrome and the associated gene mutation.
back:
• Van der Woude syndrome
• Caused by mutations in the IRF6 (Interferon Regulatory Factor 6) gene.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
coreConcept: Midline Facial Defects and Brain Anomalies
front: Explain why a median cleft lip is frequently associated with holoprosencephaly and cognitive impairment.
back:
• Both arise from a deficiency of midline tissue
• This failure occurs during neurulation, affecting the establishment of the forebrain midline and frontonasal prominence.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: Contrast the embryological origin of the primary palate with that of the lateral portions of the upper lip.
back:
• Primary palate: From the intermaxillary segment (merged medial nasal prominences)
• Lateral upper lip: Directly from the maxillary prominences.

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: State the gender predilection for cleft lip (with or without cleft palate) compared to isolated cleft palate.
back:
• Cleft lip (± palate): More common in males (~65%)
• Isolated cleft palate: More common in females (~55%).

category: Describe the development of lip and their associated congenital malformations
front: The philtrum of the upper lip is formed by the fusion of the two [___] nasal prominences.
back: medial
